feature: Persistent bottom tab bar as the primary navigation model
appleBehavior: iOS 26 restored a persistent floating tab bar (Library / Collections / Search) after iOS 18 deleted it to severe, sustained backlash; Federighi from the WWDC stage: 'Many of you missed using tabs.' The durable lesson is behavioral: ship a persistent tab bar and never take it away.
userImpact: Users get the stable, predictable, always-present navigation Apple's iOS 18 removal violated — we start on the right side of the loudest Photos usability controversy.
feasibilityNote: Already shipped as a 4-tab RN navigator (Library/Search/Albums/Desktop). Nothing to close.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation

feature: One-tap access to user Albums (Albums as a top-level destination)
appleBehavior: Apple has NO Albums tab — Albums is a row you must scroll to inside Collections (3+ taps). Losing the dedicated Albums tab is the #1 named complaint of the iOS 18 redesign and iOS 26 did NOT fix it; the only workaround (pin it) is undiscoverable.
userImpact: We put albums one tap away for the manual-organizer segment Apple alienated — instant, concrete differentiation against current Photos.
feasibilityNote: Already a dedicated bottom tab. Atlas §1.18 names this exact one-tap-Albums gap as a straight win over Apple.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation

feature: Liquid Glass floating/translucent tab bar with scroll-driven morph
appleBehavior: The iOS 26 tab bar is translucent (photos show through), floats above content, and auto-hides/morphs on scroll; in Library the morph swaps the tab bar for a bottom Years/Months/All segmented control while keeping Search bottom-right.
gap: Our tab bar is an opaque RN bar — no translucency, no float, no scroll morph, and no Years/Months/All segmented control for it to morph into.
userImpact: The app reads as visually dated next to iOS 26 and structurally different from Photos; the missing morph is coupled to the missing zoom scopes.
feasibilityNote: Native UIKit/SwiftUI apps get Liquid Glass free by recompiling with the iOS 26 SDK; an Expo RN JS tab bar does not — needs a native tab module (e.g. react-native-bottom-tabs / SwiftUI bridge) plus expo-blur for translucency (a native dep + rebuild). Current stack has no blur/haptics.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Liquid-Glass tab bar: the bottom bar background is now a real expo-blur <BlurView> (dark tint) under a translucent scrim, with an OPAQUE fallback under Reduce Transparency; taps pass through (pointerEvents none, buttons on top) and the colour-morph pills are unaffected. Reviewed clean on correctness. HONEST CAVEAT: the bar stays IN-FLOW (not a floating overlay), so the frost samples the dark app background and reads subtle — a dramatic content-blur needs a FLOATING bar, which was tried + reverted because a floating bar covers the app's bottom-anchored in-screen UI (e.g. the Library select-mode action bar); that restructure is deferred.

feature: Collections tab — the intelligent-collections hub (11 sections)
appleBehavior: A second primary tab stacking 11 auto-generated sections: Pinned, Recent Days, People & Pets, Memories, Trips, Featured Photos, Wallpaper Suggestions, Albums, Shared Albums, Media Types, Utilities — the on-device curation layer that defines modern Photos.
gap: No Collections destination at all. Our Albums tab holds only month groups + Favorites + Duplicates + real device albums; none of the intelligent sections are presented as a browsable hub.
userImpact: Users lose the entire curation layer (trips, memories, media-type and utility browsing, day clusters) that Apple foregrounds as its differentiation.
feasibilityNote: The hub shell + the easy sections (Media Types, day/month groups, Duplicates) are native-buildable; Memories/People/Featured curation is native-hard or needs-desktop; a few rows (Recently Deleted, Recovered, iCloud shared scope) are structurally blocked — see per-section rows below.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Shipped a 5th "For You" tab: an auto-Memories carousel (On-This-Day/One-Year-Ago/Recent-Favorites/Best-of-Month/Year-in-Review) + a Featured Photos highlights grid + memory drill-in, reusing PhotoGrid + MemoriesCarousel. Reviewed → fixed a P1 recycle-key. Not the full 11 auto-sections (People/Places/Trips/Media-type sections) — those need desktop/native indices.

feature: Search reachable from every view, scoped to the current album/collection
appleBehavior: Search is a system UISearchTab reachable from Library, Collections, and within a specific album/collection; typing scopes results to that container. On entry it shows suggestion chips for dates, people, and locations.
gap: We have a dedicated Search tab (scope All/Favorites only), but cannot launch search from within an album/collection and offer no in-context scoping; on-entry suggestions are recent-query chips only (no date/people/location suggestions).
userImpact: Users can't 'search just this album/trip'; they must leave context and re-filter mentally, and get no proactive date/person/place suggestions.
feasibilityNote: Passing a collection scope into our existing CLIP query path is straightforward; date-chip suggestions native-easy; people-chip suggestions needs-desktop (no on-device person graph).
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Search reachable from the tab bar everywhere, AND now SCOPED search within an album drill-in (gap 175: date/caption/keyword filter inside the opened album). A Library-vs-Collections global scope toggle is the only remaining slice.

feature: Library time-scope pyramid: Years / Months / All
appleBehavior: Three scopes; Years and Months are curated (they hide similar photos, screenshots, whiteboards, receipts) to show 'best shots'; only All is exhaustive. Tapping Years/Months jumps you to a point in time.
gap: Single newest-first exhaustive grid only — no Years/Months aggregation, no time-jump navigation, no curated best-of scope.
userImpact: Navigating a large library by time is slow; there is no way to zoom out to a year and drill in, the core Photos time-travel gesture.
feasibilityNote: Date bucketing into Years/Months is native-easy (creation_date already in our replica); the curated best-shot suppression behind Years/Months is native-hard (needs an aesthetic scorer + junk classifier — no PhotoKit API). We could ship honest uncurated scopes cheaply.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Library All/Months/Years scope segmented + live-derived period drill-ins.

feature: Adjustable grid density (pinch-to-zoom, Zoom In / Zoom Out)
appleBehavior: Pinch the grid to change thumbnail size; View Options also offers explicit Zoom In / Zoom Out.
gap: Density is fixed at 4 columns — no pinch, no zoom-in/out controls.
userImpact: Users can't trade detail for overview; power users who scan densely and those who want larger thumbnails are both stuck at one density.
feasibilityNote: Pinch + column recompute is doable on FlashList, but our documented recycle-misorder gotcha means density changes must remount the list cleanly via a key. No native dep required.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Adjustable grid density via PINCH-TO-ZOOM (Apple's Zoom In/Out): a react-native-gesture-handler Gesture.Pinch() wrapping the Library grid steps `cols` through DENSITIES [3,4,5,7] on pinch-end (spread=bigger tiles/fewer cols; pinch=more). Now buildable because gesture-handler arbitrates the 2-finger pinch against the FlashList 1-finger scroll cleanly (a plain PanResponder was screen-global and hijacked scroll -- the wall). Wired + renders on the sim, no crash. Reviewed -> fixed P3 (reset scrollY on the grid remount so the fast-scrub overlay isn't stranded over the header after a pinch). The pinch feel wants a final on-device pass.

feature: Aspect Ratio Grid vs Square Photo Grid toggle
appleBehavior: View Options toggles between square thumbnails and thumbnails shown in their native captured aspect ratio.
gap: Fixed square-ish 4-col grid; no aspect-ratio option.
userImpact: Panoramas and portraits are cropped in the grid; some users strongly prefer true-aspect thumbnails.
feasibilityNote: Pure layout using PHAsset pixelWidth/pixelHeight, already available as width/height via expo-media-library.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Library toolbar Square/Aspect toggle → FlashList masonry aspect-ratio grid.

feature: View Options content-hide toggles (Screenshots / Shared with You / From My Mac / Shared Library Badge)
appleBehavior: Toggles that hide screenshots, Messages 'Shared with You' items, Mac-synced items, and the iCloud-Shared-Library badge from the grid.
gap: No content-hide toggles of any kind.
userImpact: Screenshot and shared-item clutter can't be hidden inline while browsing.
feasibilityNote: Hide-Screenshots is native-easy (photoScreenshot subtype / the Screenshots smart album we already read); From-My-Mac via PHAsset.sourceType; Shared-with-You needs the Shared with You framework (native module); the Shared Library Badge is iCloud-Shared-Library-only (blocked-cloud).
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Hide Screenshots shipped (persisted Library exclusion of the device Screenshots album); Shared-with-You / From-My-Mac hides need iCloud/Mac provenance we do not ingest.

feature: Library sort: Recently Added vs Date Captured
appleBehavior: Two sort modes; Date Captured reorders by true capture date rather than import date (otherwise imported/AirDropped photos land at 'today').
gap: Date-descending only; no sort control and no Recently-Added vs Date-Captured distinction.
userImpact: Imported/edited/AirDropped photos jump to the top with no way to re-sort by their real capture date — a point of constant confusion even in Apple's app.
feasibilityNote: PhotoKit exposes both creationDate and modificationDate; our SQLite replica can index and toggle both. Trivial.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Date-captured asc/desc shipped; add-date not ingested.

feature: Library Filter (Favorites, Edited, Photos, Videos, Not in an Album; combinable)
appleBehavior: Combinable filters (e.g. Photos + Edited); 'All Items' clears them.
gap: No Library filter at all — Search offers only a non-combinable All/Favorites scope, and nothing filters the grid itself.
userImpact: Can't isolate favorites, un-albumed, or edited photos while browsing the grid.
feasibilityNote: Predicate filters over our replica are easy for Favorites and Not-in-Album; Videos and Edited are effectively moot because we ingest images only and track no edit state (a prerequisite gap).
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Library media-type filter shipped (All/Photos/Videos/Favorites, persisted). The remaining predicates are each blocked or a refinement: an "Edited" filter needs hasAdjustments, which expo-media-library does not expose; "Not-in-Album" needs album membership plumbed into the Library screen (asset-only today, same cost as gap 84); multi-predicate combine needs a multi-select filter-model refactor.

feature: Grid/collection toolbar controls (Sort-and-Filter, Layout-and-Reorder, More)
appleBehavior: Three distinct, context-dependent toolbar controls drive sort/filter/view-options, layout/reorder, and per-item actions; which one holds a given feature depends on where you are (e.g. Show Map lives under two of them).
gap: The Library grid has NO toolbar controls whatsoever — only multi-select batch actions exist, and per-photo actions live in the viewer rather than a grid More button.
userImpact: There is no entry point from the grid to any sort, filter, view-option, or layout affordance.
feasibilityNote: Standard header buttons + action sheets. Atlas notes Apple's own three-control split is undiscoverable — we can surface these as persistent first-class chips and beat Apple on discoverability.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Grid toolbar "More" overflow menu: a "···" button opens a small modal sheet CONSOLIDATING existing controls (Square/Aspect layout, Hide-Screenshots, Sort direction, enter Select) — each toggles the existing state + closes; accessibilityViewIsModal + onAccessibilityEscape wired. Sort/Filter/density/layout inline controls all preserved. Reviewed CLEAN. (A full drag-to-reorder collection Layout is a separate large surface.)

feature: Collections layout sizing (Large/Small/Mixed tiles) + collapse-all / per-section collapse
appleBehavior: The Layout-and-Reorder button toggles three tile sizes; Collapse All hides all tiles; a per-section chevron collapses a single section (a collapsed section still shows its titled row).
gap: No Collections hub, hence no layout sizing or collapse — and no layout/density options anywhere in the app.
userImpact: Users can't tune the information density of the curation hub (which doesn't exist yet).
feasibilityNote: Pure view-state once a Collections hub exists.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: For-You tab has a Featured-grid density control (Large/Medium/Small) + a collapse-Memories (grid-only) toggle, persisted. Reviewed clean. Mixed-tile layouts + per-section collapse are a distinct layout-engine refinement, not undertaken.

feature: Pinned Collections (user-curated pinned row of albums / media types / people / memories)
appleBehavior: Pin/unpin/reorder favorite collections and albums; default pins are Recently Saved + Favorites; the pinnable object set is fixed (albums, media types, utilities, memories, individual people/pets).
gap: No pinning or reordering of anything, anywhere in the app.
userImpact: No way to bring frequently-used albums/searches to the top; this is a feature Apple users actively ask for and often never discover.
feasibilityNote: Own pin model in SQLite. Atlas flags an easy way to beat Apple: pin saved searches, faces, date ranges, and folders — object types Apple's pinning can't hold.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Pinned Collections: a "Pinned" row at the top of Albums for go-to device/smart albums, one JSON pref (albums.pinned), resolve-not-prune, pin/unpin via long-press menu, pruned on real delete. Reviewed → fixed orphan-pin cleanup.

feature: Reorder and show/hide auto-generated sections ('grid-only' mode)
appleBehavior: iOS 26 allows only Reorder + collapse and REMOVED iOS 18's ability to hide/exclude sections; a collapsed section still occupies a titled row, and automatic grouping cannot be fully turned off (MacObserver). Still absent in iOS 27 beta.
gap: We have no section reorder/show-hide because we have no multi-section hub — but note Apple itself lost the hide capability, leaving a genuine open opening.
userImpact: N/A today, but atlas §1.18 calls a real 'grid-only, no AI sections' show/hide control the single clearest product opening in the entire IA — high documented demand Apple refuses to serve.
feasibilityNote: Trivial view-state once a hub exists. We-lead potential: ship per-section show/hide plus a clean grid-only mode.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Show/hide the auto-generated For-You sections: per-section persisted toggles (show Memories / show Featured) generalize the old collapse-Memories — hiding Featured drops its grid + density/shuffle controls, hiding both shows a hint state; sits BELOW the master "Show Featured Content" switch (gap 148). Reviewed CLEAN. (Free drag-REORDER of sections is a separate refinement.)

feature: iCloud Shared Photo Library scope picker (Both / Personal / Shared)
appleBehavior: If the user is in an iCloud Shared Photo Library, a 3-way scope picker filters what appears across all collections; buried in the Layout menu, it is the #1 cause of 'my photo disappeared' confusion.
gap: No iCloud Shared Photo Library concept and no scope picker.
userImpact: Families on a shared library can't scope their views — but this affects only Shared-Library participants.
feasibilityNote: iCloud Shared Photo Library is Apple server infrastructure; PhotoKit exposes membership read-only via source flags but not the scoping model. No local analogue beyond our own album scoping.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: iCloud Shared Photo Library is Apple server infrastructure; PhotoKit exposes membership read-only via source flags but not the scoping model. No local analogue beyond our own album scoping.

feature: Recent Days (curated day clusters) + Saved Today
appleBehavior: Day-clustered collections that open to a curated 'best of the day' summary (Show All reveals everything), plus a separate Saved Today collection below.
gap: We group by month (created_at) but have no day clusters, no per-day best-of summary, and no Saved Today.
userImpact: Recent activity isn't surfaced day-by-day the way Photos foregrounds it at the top of Collections.
feasibilityNote: Day bucketing is native-easy; the curated day summary needs an aesthetic scorer (native-hard). Saved-Today via a recently-added query is native-easy.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Recent Days (day clusters) + SAVED TODAY: the Recent-Days utility shipped earlier; "Saved Today" now added as an Albums Utility row (photos whose capture day = today, `new Date()` at runtime, gated to >=1 today-photo) drilling into its own grid, mirroring the Recently-Added pattern. Reviewed clean (P3 midnight-staleness matches the sibling utilities' convention; accepted).

feature: People & Pets collection + Groups (browsable on-device people/pet graph)
appleBehavior: On-device face + pet recognition with co-occurrence grouping, per-person key photos, naming, favoriting, hide/de-feature, and custom sort — a top-level browsable people surface. The atlas calls People the single most important section of Photos.
gap: No People/Pets browse hub in the app IA. Face recognition exists ONLY as a per-photo 'Recognize' action against the paired desktop oracle — there is no phone-native people album, no groups, no person-centric browsing/naming/co-occurrence.
userImpact: Users cannot browse or manage 'photos of a person' — the most-used organizational surface in all of Photos is absent from the phone IA.
feasibilityNote: PHPerson is not public, so even Apple's own graph is unreachable; identities require our licensed desktop oracle (or native-hard on-device Vision face clustering). The browse-hub IA is native-easy once identities exist. We already LEAD on correctability (desktop oracle + Platt/AS-Norm/cross-age decision layer, which Apple has zero of) — the gap here is purely the phone-side people IA surface.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Only feasible via the paired desktop oracle (out of the mobile app’s scope). PHPerson is not public, so even Apple's own graph is unreachable; identities require our licensed desktop oracle (or native-hard on-device Vision face clustering). The browse-hub I

feature: Memories (auto-curated collections + memory movies) and Favorite Memories
appleBehavior: Personalized collections around a significant person/pet/place/activity/event, playable memory movies with licensed music, event-named in iOS 26, and favoritable into a Favorite Memories sub-collection.
gap: We show a client-side Memories carousel header (On This Day, Recent Favorites) but there is no full Memories collection, no themed compilations, no memory movies, and no Favorite Memories.
userImpact: The nostalgic resurfacing layer is thin — no movies, no themed memories, no favoriting of memories.
feasibilityNote: On-This-Day we already have (native-easy). Themed curation is native-hard; memory movies need video composition AND soundtrack licensing (Apple sidesteps this via Apple Music) — a real blocker. Atlas notes Apple's memory-suppression UX is its worst; a respectful 'what should I resurface' control is a trust win.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Auto-curated Memories (On-This-Day/One-Year-Ago/Recent-Favorites/Best-of-Month/Year-in-Review) + Ken-Burns slideshow + edit/remove/reorder shipped; memory MOVIES (video montage) not.

feature: Trips (location-clustered travel collections)
appleBehavior: Spatio-temporal clustering of geotagged assets into named trips, with a year filter; GPS-less photos are silently excluded, and there is no way to create, rename, merge, or split a trip.
gap: No Trips and no location-based grouping of any kind.
userImpact: No automatic 'this trip' grouping — one of the most beloved Photos organization features is absent.
feasibilityNote: Clustering is easy IF we have per-asset GPS, but our on-device AssetInfo exposes no location/EXIF (documented gotcha) — coordinates must come from the desktop EXIF oracle or a native module reading PHAsset.location; reverse-geocode names via a native geocoder. Atlas: Trips is one of the easiest Apple collections to BEAT (Apple offers zero trip editing).
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation

feature: Featured Photos collection
appleBehavior: An on-device auto-selected 'best/featured photos' section in Collections, suppressible only via Show Featured Content.
gap: No Featured Photos surface (our 'Recent Favorites' is favorites-only, not aesthetic featuring).
userImpact: No serendipitous best-of resurfacing on the browse surface.
feasibilityNote: Needs an aesthetic scorer (no PhotoKit API); could reuse CLIP-based scoring. Since Apple only lets you suppress-not-tune it, a cleaner control is a small win.

closureNote: Featured Photos collection: the favorites-first, recent-padded, deduped/capped, day-rotating Featured grid is the body of the For-You tab (gap 143). Shipped.

feature: Wallpaper Suggestions collection
appleBehavior: An on-device collection suggesting photos suitable for wallpaper — a fully wired Collections destination with its own guide page.

userImpact: Minor — a curation/utility flourish; users can't get wallpaper picks or set one from our app.
feasibilityNote: Suggesting candidates is buildable, but setting Lock/Home Screen wallpaper is a private/system capability third-party apps cannot perform — the payoff action is blocked, capping the feature's value.

domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Panoramas row (aspect proxy) + Screenshots/Selfies device albums; true Portrait/Live/RAW/Slo-mo need mediaSubtype/video we do not ingest.

feature: Utilities grab-bag (Recently Saved/Viewed/Shared/Edited, Imports, Duplicates, Hidden, Recently Deleted, Favorites, Recovered + semantic Documents/Receipts/Handwriting/Illustrations/QR Codes)
appleBehavior: A catch-all Collections row of activity, system, and on-device content-classified utility collections.
gap: We have Duplicates and Favorites; we lack Recently Viewed/Shared/Edited, Imports, Hidden, Recently Deleted, Recovered, and every semantic utility (Documents/Receipts/Handwriting/Illustrations/QR Codes).

feasibilityNote: Duplicates we already ship and BEAT Apple on (Apple's Duplicates is famously unfindable). Semantic utilities are rebuildable with Vision (VNRecognizeTextRequest, document detection, VNDetectBarcodesRequest) — native-moderate, likely needs a native Vision module in Expo. Recently Deleted and Recovered are blocked-platform (no PhotoKit API).
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Albums Utilities (Recently Added, Recent Days, Panoramas) shipped; Recently-Viewed/Shared/Imports need data we lack.

feature: Hidden album
appleBehavior: smartAlbumAllHidden, biometric-locked by default; a Show Hidden Album setting can remove it from Photos entirely.
gap: No Hidden view — no way to move sensitive photos out of the main grid.
userImpact: Sensitive photos always appear in the newest-first grid with no hide affordance.
feasibilityNote: smartAlbumAllHidden is fetchable via PhotoKit; biometric lock via expo-local-authentication. Our SQLCipher-encrypted replica already gives at-rest protection, so we can match and arguably exceed Apple for our own hidden set.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: App-local Hidden album: hide from Library select mode → photo is partitioned out of Library/Search(+CLIP/OCR)/Albums(months/Favorites/Utilities/device-albums)/Memories/Duplicates and shown only in the Hidden view (select → Unhide back into the library). Replica is_hidden flag, instant optimistic Set + Undo. App-local only (PhotoKit gives 3rd parties no Hidden access); no biometric lock yet. Adversarially reviewed → fixed a P1 leak (hidden photos were surfacing in the Duplicates review → excluded from clustering).

feasibilityNote: PhotoKit exposes NO Recently Deleted collection to third parties — surfacing Apple's trash in-app is structurally impossible. Best local analogue: our own soft-delete/trash layer for deletions initiated within our app.

closureNote: PhotoKit exposes NO Recently Deleted collection to third parties — surfacing Apple's trash in-app is structurally impossible. Best local analogue: our own soft-delete/trash layer for deletions initiated within our app.

gap: No Recovered surface.

feature: Per-collection biometric lock (Face ID / Touch ID / passcode on Hidden & Recently Deleted)
appleBehavior: Hidden and Recently Deleted are locked by default; unlocked via biometrics/passcode; togglable in Settings.
gap: No biometric-lock UI on any view (although the entire SQLite replica is SQLCipher-encrypted at rest).
userImpact: No quick shoulder-surf protection for a hidden/sensitive subset while the app is open.

Reviewed clean. WARNING expo-local-authentication is native -> needs npx expo prebuild + an iOS rebuild; tsc-verified only. (There is no app-side Recently-Deleted surface to also lock.)

gap: The Albums tab has NO create/rename/delete, no folders, no Personal/Shared/Activity segmentation, and no album sort/filter/view-format. New-album creation exists only from the photo viewer via an iOS Alert.prompt; rename, delete, and folders are absent everywhere.

appleBehavior: A top-right avatar menu on the Collections tab holds the de-facto Photos preferences: curation toggles, autoplay/loop control, and the People & Pets reset.
gap: No account or settings menu anywhere in the app — there is zero user-facing preferences surface.
userImpact: Users have no place to control curation, autoplay, resets, or any preference; the app is entirely settings-less.
feasibilityNote: A settings screen is trivial to add; the specific toggles map to curation/autoplay features we'd first have to build. Atlas notes Apple's split-brain settings (avatar menu vs Settings app) are a weakness we can beat with one clear settings home.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: A Settings surface exists (reached from Albums) and already hosts the Show-Featured-Content toggle; reshaping it into an avatar/account menu is a cosmetic re-presentation of an existing surface — no new capability.

feature: Event recognition + event details panel (concerts / sports)
appleBehavior: iOS 26 recognizes concert and sport events; a ticket button replaces the info button and opens set lists / scores / upcoming events, and memories are named after the specific event. There is no way to correct a misidentified event.
gap: No event recognition and no event details panel.
userImpact: No rich event context on photos — a niche, region- and catalog-limited feature.
feasibilityNote: Requires third-party data licensing (Ticketmaster / setlist.fm / sports feeds) plus geo+time inference; Apple has a structural advantage via Apple Music. Not on-device-buildable without external services.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Requires third-party data licensing (Ticketmaster / setlist.fm / sports feeds) plus geo+time inference; Apple has a structural advantage via Apple Music. Not on-device-buildable without external services.

feature: Star ratings (1–5) + keywords with filter-by-rating (iOS 27 beta)
appleBehavior: iOS 27 (beta; ships fall 2026) adds 1–5 star ratings and keywords on photos/videos, filterable by rating — Apple's first genuinely metadata-driven organization.
gap: No ratings, keywords, or tags.
userImpact: Power organizers can't rate, tag, or keyword-filter — and Apple only ships this this fall, so there is a closing first-mover window.
feasibilityNote: Our SQLite replica can store ratings/keywords/tags today, with XMP-sidecar import/export as the interop story. Atlas §1.17 flags that it is UNKNOWN whether Apple exposes these via PhotoKit; if not, Apple builds a metadata lock-in moat and we should ship ratings/keywords immediately. We-lead potential.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Star ratings (1-5) + keywords + filter-by-rating: all shipped — rating input in the viewer (replica-stored), the Library "Rated" filter (gap 66), and the keyword chip filter/browse (gap 67). Complete.

feature: iOS 27 Utilities additions: Captured by Me + Identity Documents
appleBehavior: iOS 27 beta adds a 'Captured by Me' utility (photos taken on your own iPhone cameras, excluding Messages/AirDrop/shared) and an 'Identity Documents' utility that aggregates passports, licenses, and IDs.
gap: Neither utility exists.
userImpact: No own-camera filter, and no auto-rounded-up ID-document view (nor its privacy risk).
feasibilityNote: Captured-by-Me is native-easy (sourceType user-library + camera EXIF). Identity Documents needs a Vision document classifier (native-moderate). Atlas warns Identity Documents is a trust liability Apple voluntarily takes on — a privacy-forward version should be opt-in, locked, and strictly on-device; we-lead potential on that framing.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation
closureNote: Infeasible for a 3rd-party app: capture-source "Captured by Me" + holiday-event metadata iOS does not expose; PhotoKit forbids non-destructive in-place edit (adjustmentData/Revert); intra-video key-moment CLIP needs a native frame-extraction pipeline; Android Motion Photo is N/A on iOS.

feature: Paired-desktop uplink as a top-level navigation destination
appleBehavior: No Apple equivalent — Photos has no concept of pairing to a trusted desktop that computes heavyweight ML the phone can't.
userImpact: From the phone, users browse the desktop catalog, run full-library desktop search, get licensed per-photo face recognition, and read desktop EXIF — capabilities the phone cannot compute locally and Apple offers nowhere.
feasibilityNote: Already shipped (SEC-09 companion HTTP: pair → catalog → desktop previews → face-recognition oracle, cookie auth). A structural advantage with no Apple analogue.
domain: Information Architecture & Navigation

feature: Persistent bottom tab bar / where Library sits (Library + Collections + Search)
appleBehavior: iOS 26 restored a 2-tab Liquid-Glass tab bar (Library | Collections) plus a separate bottom Search button after the iOS 18 no-tab-bar redesign became the app's loudest-ever backlash; the tab bar morphs into a nav bar exposing Months/Years on scroll.
userImpact: We ship exactly what Apple's users begged for and a $5 third-party app (Photon Library) existed to restore: a conventional, always-present tab bar that never disappears. Our 4 tabs (Library/Search/Albums/Desktop) put browsing one tap away.
feasibilityNote: Already implemented; the lesson from the atlas is behavioral (never remove the tab bar), which we satisfy. No work needed.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing

feature: Library zoom hierarchy: Years / Months / All levels
appleBehavior: Pull down on the grid to reveal three levels — Years, Months, All. Months clusters by 'significant events' (on-device spatiotemporal+content clustering); Years/Months are curated 'best shots'. Only All shows the complete library. (The classic 4-level Years/Months/Days/All pyramid is gone; Days was cut.)
gap: We have exactly one level — a flat newest-first grid. No Years, no Months, no event clustering, no way to pull-down to a higher-altitude time view.
userImpact: Users with large libraries cannot zoom out to a year/month overview to navigate time; every trip back in time is a long scroll. This is a core Apple browsing primitive we entirely lack.
feasibilityNote: Date-bucketed Year/Month section levels are straightforward over our SQLite created_at index + FlashList section headers (no native dep). The 'significant events' clustering is the hard part but a simple date-gap heuristic gets 80%. The aesthetic 'best shots' curation is separate (see next row).
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Library All/Months/Years scope + period drill-ins.

feature: Curated 'best shots' Years/Months view (suppresses screenshots, near-dupes, whiteboards, receipts)
appleBehavior: Years and Months apply an opaque on-device aesthetic/curation score to show only 'best shots' and actively hide clutter. Apple exposes no API and no user control, and this silently-lossy default drives a large share of 'my photos are missing' complaints.
userImpact: We show every photo, every time — no silent suppression. The atlas explicitly names 'invert the default: complete by default, curation opt-in' as the winning move, which is our current behavior by default. We lead on trust/honesty here.
feasibilityNote: We already win by being complete-by-default. Adding an OPT-IN curated view (score + hide clutter) would need an on-device aesthetic model; CLIP embeddings we already compute + a screenshot/receipt classifier could approximate it. Worth an always-visible 'N hidden by curation — show' affordance if we ever add it. PhotoKit ships no such API (verified via atlas §2.19).
domain: Library & Grid Browsing

feature: Grid thumbnail density: pinch-to-zoom + View Options Zoom In / Zoom Out
appleBehavior: Two mechanisms change density: pinch the grid, or More → View Options → repeatable Zoom In / Zoom Out. Multiple discrete densities exist (count undocumented; iOS 26.2.1 reduced the max zoom-out to ~45 thumbnails, a regression users complained about).
gap: Our grid is FIXED at 4 columns. No pinch-to-change-density, no zoom-in/out control, no way to see more or fewer thumbnails.
userImpact: Pinch-to-zoom density is one of the most-used browsing gestures in Photos; users can't get a denser overview for fast scanning or a larger view for detail. A jarring miss vs muscle memory.
feasibilityNote: Pure RN: a numColumns state (e.g. 2/3/4/5/7) driven by a PinchGestureHandler, with expo-image requesting proportional target sizes to avoid memory thrash. No native module or rebuild needed. Persist the chosen density.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Density control (cycles 3/4/5/7 cols) in Library.

feature: Aspect Ratio Grid vs Square Photo Grid
appleBehavior: More → View Options toggles between square center-cropped 1:1 thumbnails and a native-aspect masonry/mosaic grid. (Apple's own doc even has a typo, 'Aspect Ration Grid'.)
gap: We render one grid style only (uniform cells). No aspect-ratio/masonry mode, no square-vs-native toggle.
userImpact: Photographers who want to see true framing (tall portraits, panoramas) can't; everything is uniformly cropped. Niche but valued by the manual-organizer segment.
feasibilityNote: PHAsset.pixelWidth/pixelHeight (exposed by expo-media-library asset info) give native aspect WITHOUT loading pixels, so a masonry layout is cheap to compute up front. No native dep.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Library toolbar Square/Aspect toggle → FlashList masonry aspect-ratio grid.

feature: View Options content-hiding toggles (Screenshots / Shared with You / From My Mac / Shared Library Badge)
appleBehavior: Four persistent de-clutter toggles that durably hide screenshots, Messages-shared items, Mac-synced items, and the shared-library badge from the grid. Distinct from temporary Filters.
gap: No content-hiding toggles at all. Screenshots and every other image type are always mixed into our one grid with no way to durably exclude a class.
userImpact: Users who want a screenshot-free library (a frequent request) can't get one. We ingest screenshots indiscriminately with no exclusion.
feasibilityNote: PHAssetMediaSubtype.photoScreenshot and PHAssetSourceType are surfaced by expo-media-library; we can offer MORE granular exclusions than Apple's four. Pure query-predicate work over our replica.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Hide Screenshots shipped; Shared-with-You / From-My-Mac content-hide toggles need iCloud/Mac data we lack.

feature: Library sort: Sort by Recently Added / Sort by Date Captured (+ direction)
appleBehavior: Exactly two sort options in the Library More menu. Newest lands at the BOTTOM and there is NO newest-first/oldest-first direction toggle for the Library (that only exists inside albums). Recently Added = added-date; Date Captured = EXIF date.
gap: We hard-code date-descending on created_at only. No Recently-Added vs Date-Captured choice, no ascending/descending toggle, and we don't distinguish added-date from capture-date.
userImpact: Users can't switch between 'stuff I just imported/AirDropped' (added-date) and true chronological (capture-date) — the exact confusion Apple's own two modes address. No sort control is a basic-browser miss.
feasibilityNote: PHAsset exposes creationDate, addedDate, and modificationDate; expo-media-library gives creation/modification time, and we can persist added-date at ingest. We can ship BOTH Apple modes PLUS the ascending/descending direction toggle Apple withholds — an afternoon of sortDescriptor work. Potential we-lead.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Date-captured asc/desc shipped; "Recently Added" needs an add-date we do not ingest.

feature: Library Filter (Photos / Videos / Favorites / Edited / Not in an Album, combinable, temporary)
appleBehavior: More → Filter narrows the grid to combinations (e.g. Photos + Edited). 'Not in an Album' is a beloved cleanup filter with no PhotoKit equivalent. Filters are temporary and can't be saved as a smart view (an Apple weakness).
gap: No filter on the Library grid at all. (Search has an All/Favorites scope, but that is the semantic-search surface, not a grid filter, and offers only two values.)
userImpact: No way to see only videos, only edited, only favorites, or the cleanup-critical 'Not in an Album' while browsing. Library-hygiene workflows are impossible.
feasibilityNote: isFavorite and hasAdjustments map to fields we can store; mediaType filters need video ingestion first (see media row). 'Not in an Album' has no predicate anywhere — compute the set difference against album memberships, cheap over SQLite. We could also ship SAVED filters (persistent smart views) that Apple lacks — a we-lead.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Library media-type filter shipped (All/Photos/Videos/Favorites, videos ingested, folded into gridKey + time-scope + empty state, persisted). Remaining: "Edited" needs hasAdjustments (not exposed by expo-media-library); "Not-in-Album" needs album membership in the Library screen (same plumbing as gap 84); multi-combine needs a multi-select filter refactor.

feature: Viewer filmstrip scrubber (thumbnail strip under the open photo)
appleBehavior: In the full-screen viewer a horizontal thumbnail strip sits below the photo; swiping it jumps forward/back quickly, synchronized with the paged viewer.
gap: Our viewer supports swipe-paging one photo at a time but has no filmstrip scrubber to skim rapidly across many photos.
userImpact: To move far within a burst of viewing (dozens of photos) users must swipe one-by-one instead of scrubbing the strip. Slower navigation inside the viewer.
feasibilityNote: A horizontal FlashList of thumbnails bound to the pager index; pure RN, no native dep. We already load the ordered asset list for paging.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Viewer bottom-chrome thumbnail strip (virtualized FlatList): active thumb ring + auto-centre, tap/drag to jump the pager; hides with chrome, off over info/editor. Reviewed (P3 centre-offset fixed).

feature: Grid fast-scroll scrubber + jump-to-date + floating date bubble
appleBehavior: There is NO date-labelled scroll rail and NO jump-to-date in Apple's grid; a plain scroll indicator exists but rapid-scroll-to-end regressed in iOS 18 and users still complain. Per the atlas this is 'the highest-value, lowest-effort win in the entire domain' — Apple is weak here.
gap: We have no fast-scroll scrubber, no jump-to-date, no floating year/month bubble — only pull-to-refresh and plain scrolling.
userImpact: Scrolling-to-find-an-image is the dominant Photos use case; on a large library our flat grid becomes an endless scroll with no way to jump to a date. This is where we could BEAT Apple, and currently we merely match their weakness.
feasibilityNote: A grabbable right-edge scrubber with a date bubble over FlashList is achievable in RN Animated (we deliberately avoid reanimated); needs a custom overlay tracking scroll offset → date bucket from our indexed created_at. Neither Apple nor we have it — a clear we-lead opportunity, verified as Apple's #1 gap in atlas §2.20.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Library flat-grid gets the Apple fast-scrub handle: a right-edge draggable thumb → jumps the grid to that capture-month (FlashList scrollToIndex) with a floating month bubble (reuses DateScrubber). Only activates once scrolled into the grid rows (box-none/opacity gated on scroll offset vs header) so it never hijacks the top Memories card; hidden while selecting. Reviewed → fixed the P2 header-touch-hijack.

feature: Video, Live Photo & burst ingestion + playback in the library
appleBehavior: The Library shows and plays every media type — videos (tap to play, scrub bar), Live Photos (touch-and-hold to play), and burst stacks — all inline in the grid and viewer.
gap: Our ingest queries MediaType.IMAGE ONLY. No videos, Live Photos, or bursts are ingested AT ALL, so none appear in the grid and none can play in the viewer. Entire media classes are invisible in our app.
userImpact: A user whose library is 30% video/Live Photos opens our Library and simply doesn't see them — the single most jarring completeness gap vs Apple. For a 'browse my whole library' companion this reads as broken/incomplete.
feasibilityNote: Query change to include MediaType.VIDEO is trivial; inline video playback via expo-video (thumbnail + tap-to-play) is native-moderate; Live Photo playback needs PHLivePhotoView, i.e. a small native module + a dev-client rebuild (we currently ship pure RN Animated, no such module). Burst stacks are readable via PHAsset.burstIdentifier. Foundational — gates the Videos filter and autoplay rows.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Video ingest + playback shipped (expo-video, needs rebuild); Live Photos + burst stacking not yet.

feature: Motion autoplay: Auto-Play Motion / Loop Videos
appleBehavior: By default Live Photos and short videos auto-play as you scroll Collections; Loop Videos restarts a video at its end. Both are user-toggleable (account button and Settings → Photos); Loop Videos became a toggle in iOS 18.2 after complaints.
gap: N/A today because we ingest no motion media — but consequently we have neither autoplay nor its kill-switch. Once video/Live is ingested we'd need to build both.
userImpact: No motion previews while scrolling (a signature Apple feel). Conversely, once we add motion we'd need the autoplay OFF control that motion-sensitive users need — we already support Reduce-Motion, a good foundation.
feasibilityNote: Depends entirely on the video/Live ingestion row. Autoplay-on-scroll for videos is doable with expo-video visibility tracking; battery/thermal cost is real (atlas warns) so gate it behind a toggle and Reduce-Motion, which we honor.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Loop Videos toggle shipped in the viewer (persisted, live via player.loop). Auto-Play Motion (autoplaying videos inline in the grid) not — too heavy for the grid.

feature: Recent Days collection (curated day-by-day of recent photos)
appleBehavior: Collections → Recent Days (top of tab) shows recent days; opening a day shows a curated summary of 'best photos' with Show All as the escape hatch. This is where the old Days level went (recent-only, not full history).
gap: No day-level browse surface. Our Albums tab has month groups (created_at) but no per-day recent view and no day summaries.
userImpact: 'What did I shoot on Tuesday?' has no fast answer in our app; users scroll the flat grid. Lower impact than year/month levels but a real navigation axis.
feasibilityNote: Day-bucketing over our indexed created_at is trivial; we'd default to complete (no curation) which the atlas frames as the better behavior. Pure RN.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Albums Utilities: Recently Added + Recent Days (per-day) rows drilling into scoped grids.

feature: Recency collections: Recently Saved / Recently Viewed / Recently Shared / Saved Today
appleBehavior: Dedicated collections answer 'where did the photo I just saved go?' — Recently Saved (AirDrop/Messages/Safari saves), Saved Today, plus Recently Viewed and Recently Shared under Utilities.
gap: None of these recency surfaces exist. No 'recently saved', 'saved today', 'recently viewed', or 'recently shared'.
userImpact: The common 'where did the thing I just saved go?' question has no shortcut; users hunt the grid. Niche but frequently asked.
feasibilityNote: Recently Saved is approximable via smartAlbumRecentlyAdded + sourceType + addedDate (native-easy). Recently Viewed/Shared are system-tracked and NOT exposed by PhotoKit (blocked-platform for the system library) — we could only track events inside our own app.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Recently Added (Albums Utility) covers Recently Saved, and SAVED TODAY is now its own Utility row (gap 16). Only Recently VIEWED and Recently SHARED remain — they need per-asset view/share timestamps the app doesn't keep and PhotoKit doesn't expose to 3rd parties.

feature: Media Types breakdown (Portrait, Time-lapse, Slo-mo, Panorama, Live, RAW, Cinematic, Spatial, Screen Recordings, etc.)
appleBehavior: Collections → Media Types groups every capture type into browsable smart albums; reorderable and pinnable.
gap: We surface only Screenshots and Selfies smart albums (in the Albums tab). Portrait, Panorama, Slo-mo, Time-lapse, RAW, Cinematic, Spatial, Live, Bursts, Screen Recordings, Videos etc. are not exposed as a Media-Types breakdown.
userImpact: Users can't jump to 'all my Portraits' or 'all my slow-mos'. We expose a slice of the taxonomy but not the full media-type navigation.
feasibilityNote: This is 'the one curation area Apple hands you outright' (atlas §2.19): PHAssetCollectionSubtype smart albums (smartAlbumPanoramas, smartAlbumTimelapses, smartAlbumDepthEffect, smartAlbumRAW, smartAlbumCinematic, smartAlbumSpatial, …) are enumerable via expo-media-library. Most are blocked only by our images-only ingest for the video subtypes.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Panoramas row (aspect proxy) + Screenshots/Selfies device albums; true Portrait/Live/RAW/Slo-mo need mediaSubtype/video we do not ingest.

feature: Utilities content collections: Receipts / Documents / Handwriting / Illustrations / QR Codes
appleBehavior: On-device Vision classification auto-groups receipts, documents, handwriting, illustrations, and QR codes under Utilities. No way to correct a misclassification.
gap: No content-classification collections. We can't group receipts/documents/QR codes; our only content understanding is CLIP semantic search, which isn't a persistent browsable collection.
userImpact: Users can't browse 'all my receipts' or 'all my QR codes' as a folder. Our CLIP search can find them by query but there's no curated at-a-glance collection.
feasibilityNote: Fully rebuildable with Apple's Vision (VNClassifyImageRequest, VNRecognizeTextRequest, VNDetectBarcodesRequest) but Vision needs a native module + dev-client rebuild — outside our current pure-JS/executorch stack. Alternatively the paired desktop oracle could classify (needs-desktop). We could also correct misclassifications, which Apple can't — a we-lead angle.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Markup (freehand draw/shapes/text/signature) needs continuous multi-touch path tracking that can't be device-verified in this env (the gesture-verification wall) + Skia touch/gesture-handler; and Receipts/Documents/Handwriting/QR auto-collections need iOS VisionKit document/QR/handwriting classifiers with no Expo API (CLIP approximates the queries but not dedicated auto-albums).

feature: Multi-select core (Select mode + slide-to-select + bulk actions)
appleBehavior: Tap Select then tap or slide across thumbnails; iOS 26 made Select larger/always-visible. Bulk actions include Favorite, Delete, Share, Add to Album, Hide, Copy, and batch date/location edit.
gap: We HAVE Select + multi-select + batch Favorite (with Undo toast) and batch Delete. We're missing the broader batch action set: batch Add-to-Album (we only add-to-album for a single photo in the viewer), batch Share, batch Hide, Copy, and batch date/location edit.
userImpact: Core selection works, but power organizers can select many photos and then only favorite or delete them — they can't file a selection into an album or share a set in bulk. Half the value of multi-select is missing.
feasibilityNote: Batch Add-to-Album and batch Share are pure RN over expo-media-library album APIs + the system share sheet we already use. Batch date/location needs PHAssetChangeRequest (see metadata row). We already have the selection substrate and Undo toast to build on.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Multi-select core INCLUDING slide-to-select: Select mode + bulk actions shipped across Library/Hidden/album drill-ins; SLIDE-TO-SELECT now added (react-native-gesture-handler Pan over the square grid — maps the finger to a cell via scroll offset + measured header height, activeOffsetX so a VERTICAL drag still scrolls and can never break scrolling, gated to select-mode + non-masonry + surfaces with scrollY). Reviewed -> fixed P2 (interpolate the index range between samples so a fast stroke skips no cells) + P3 (anchor a single add/remove PAINT mode from the first cell + a painted-set so a back-drag doesn't reverse it). Correct-by-construction with gesture-handler; final drag FEEL wants an on-device pass. (range/by-day/invert still pending — see 53.)

feature: Select All / range-select / select-by-day / invert / selection tray (incl. iOS 27 'Show Selected')
appleBehavior: Apple has NO Select All in the main Library (a near-universal complaint), no range-select, no select-by-header; iOS 27 beta adds a 'Show Selected' review view — Apple conceding the point. Select All exists only in Duplicates/Recently Deleted.
gap: We have per-photo tapping only — no Select All, no tap-first-then-tap-last range select, no select-entire-day/month header, no invert-selection, no persistent selection tray.
userImpact: Selecting hundreds of photos is an exhausting manual tap-fest — the exact pain that spawned a genre of 'how to select all photos on iPhone' articles. Both we and Apple are weak, so shipping these would beat Apple.
feasibilityNote: Select All / range-select / select-by-day / a persistent selection tray are all pure RN state over our existing multi-select. The atlas explicitly lists these as Library wins Apple lacks — a clear we-lead opportunity.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Select-All + SLIDE-TO-SELECT (gap 52) + INVERT-selection (over the visible set) now shipped; the last refinements — range-select (shift-anchor drag) and select-by-day (a day-header select-all) — need anchor tracking / a day-grouped grid, pending.

feature: Detail viewer core: full-screen, swipe paging, pinch/double-tap zoom, tap-to-toggle chrome
appleBehavior: Tap a thumbnail → full-screen; swipe to page; pinch and double-tap to zoom within a photo; tap to hide/show controls; X to close. Well-liked — the baseline to MATCH.
userImpact: We match all of it AND add a zoom-open-from-cell shared-element transition Apple doesn't have. This is a solved, polished surface for us.
feasibilityNote: Already implemented (native pinch-zoom, swipe paging, tap-to-toggle chrome, zoom-open-from-cell). The one missing sub-piece is the filmstrip scrubber (separate row).
domain: Library & Grid Browsing

feature: Spatial Scenes (iOS 26 — 3D depth parallax from any 2D photo)
appleBehavior: Viewer hexagon icon → 'Spatial Scene': separates subject from background and adds motion as you tilt the phone. Works on any photo (even years-old), iPhone 12+, and notably does NOT require Apple Intelligence.
gap: No spatial/3D/parallax viewing effect at all.
userImpact: A delightful, showy viewer effect we lack; niche but a visible 'Apple can do this, you can't' moment.
feasibilityNote: Apple's generative depth model isn't exposed, but the atlas says it's approximatable with a monocular depth model (Core ML/Vision) + a gyro-driven parallax shader — 'very achievable and visually striking'. Needs a native module/GL work outside our current RN Animated stack, or the desktop oracle to synthesize the depth map.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Apple capture-format / hardware pipeline the OS owns (RAW/ProRAW, Portrait depth, Cinematic, Spatial/MV-HEVC, HDR gain-map, ProRes/Log, deferred photoProxy) — a 3rd-party app can't decode, render or edit these on-device; iOS exposes no public API for them.

feature: Info panel breadth (people/pets, caption, Visual Look Up, event info, device, date, camera EXIF, location map, who-shared, albums)
appleBehavior: Rich curated info panel: people & pets, editable caption, Visual Look Up results, concert/sport event info, capturing device, date/time (Adjust), camera metadata (lens/shutter/ISO/file size), location with Maps link (Adjust), who shared it, and which albums it's in.
gap: On-device we show only filename, taken date/time, dimensions+megapixels, and favorite y/n. Missing on-device: full camera EXIF, location/map, caption, Visual Look Up, event info, who-shared, and the album-membership list. People-chips + camera/place/aperture/ISO EXIF only appear WHEN a desktop is paired (desktop oracle), not standalone.
userImpact: A user without a paired desktop sees a bare info panel — no lens/ISO/aperture, no location, no map, no people. Apple shows all of this on-device for free. Our richest info requires the desktop uplink.
feasibilityNote: EXIF (lens/shutter/ISO/aperture/file size) is native-easy on-device: pull image data via expo-media-library and read CGImageSource properties (no PhotoKit EXIF on PHAsset, but the data is readable). Album-membership list is native-easy. Location+map needs a maps module (native-moderate). People & Visual Look Up have NO public API (blocked-platform) — hence our correct choice to source them from the desktop oracle (needs-desktop). Event info / who-shared are blocked-platform. We could stop gating EXIF/location behind the desktop and show it locally.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Added app-local caption + star rating to the info panel; people / Photos-caption / Visual-Look-Up still absent.

feature: Adjust Date & Time / Adjust Location (single + batch + revert)
appleBehavior: Info panel → Adjust to change capture date/time or location (with Maps text-search), individually or batched over a selection, non-destructively with Revert-to-original. No relative/timezone shift though (an Apple gap).
gap: No metadata editing whatsoever — can't fix a wrong date, can't set/adjust location, no batch, no revert.
userImpact: A trip shot with the wrong camera clock or missing GPS can't be corrected in our app; users must go to Apple Photos. A standard library-management capability we don't offer.
feasibilityNote: PHAssetChangeRequest exposes settable creationDate and location (expo-media-library supports change requests); batch = a loop in one change block. Trap: PhotoKit gives no Revert — we'd store originals ourselves. Opportunity to beat Apple with a RELATIVE '+3 hours'/timezone shift (the archetypal need Apple lacks).
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: expo-media-library exposes NO API to edit an asset's creation date or location — that is PhotoKit PHAssetChangeRequest, which Expo does not wrap; a 3rd-party Expo app can't change capture metadata (verified against the installed module's types).

feature: Caption field (free-text per-asset, indexed by Search)
appleBehavior: A per-asset caption entered in the info panel and indexed by Photos Search. iOS 27 beta adds Keywords alongside captions.
gap: No caption field; users can't annotate a photo or make it findable by their own description.
userImpact: No way to add a note/description to a photo; our search is CLIP-only so user intent ('Grandma's 80th') can't be pinned to an asset.
feasibilityNote: We can store captions in our own SQLite keyed by localIdentifier and even index them in our search — but there is a hard interop wall (atlas §2.19): PHAsset has no caption property and PHAssetChangeRequest no caption setter, so we can NEVER round-trip into Apple's caption field (blocked-platform for interop). Our own-store version is fully doable.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: App-local per-photo CAPTION field (add/edit in the viewer info panel, persisted in photo_meta) is now INDEXED BY SEARCH: replica searchCaptions() (term-AND LIKE over photo_meta.caption) is unioned into the Search results alongside CLIP ∪ OCR (deduped, mapped through the visible set). Reviewed CLEAN. (Not written to PhotoKit — it blocks 3rd-party caption writes — so it stays app-local.)

feature: Live Photo effects + editing (Loop / Bounce / Long Exposure, key photo, trim, mute, Save as Video)
appleBehavior: Open a Live Photo → Live menu → Loop / Bounce / Long Exposure; Edit lets you set key photo, trim, mute, and export as video.
gap: We ingest no Live Photos, so none of this exists — no playback, no effects, no key-photo/trim, no Save-as-Video.
userImpact: Live Photo owners get nothing from our app for that content. Batch Live-to-still conversion (a top storage request Apple itself doesn't offer) is also absent.
feasibilityNote: Requires Live Photo ingestion + PHLivePhotoView (native module/rebuild) as prerequisite, then Loop/Bounce/Long-Exposure rendering over the video track implemented ourselves. Well outside current pure-RN scope; a later native-client investment.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Live Photo effects/editing (Loop/Bounce/Long-Exposure, key-photo/trim/mute/make-still/save-as-video) need the native PHLivePhotoView + Live-Photo edit pipeline; video trim/speed-ramp/frame-grab need AVFoundation — neither is exposed by Expo (expo-video only plays standard video). Detection is possible via mediaSubtype, but this editing/motion pipeline is native-only and not buildable or verifiable here.

feature: Burst triage (stacked thumbnail, suggested keepers, keep flow)
appleBehavior: Bursts appear as one stacked thumbnail; opening shows gray-dot suggested keepers; you pick which frames to save as individual photos or delete the whole burst. Browsable under Media Types → Bursts.
gap: We ingest no bursts and offer no burst-triage flow.
userImpact: Users with hundreds of unreviewed bursts silently eating storage get no help from us (Apple never nags either). A one-tap burst cleanup is a cheap storage win we can't deliver today.
feasibilityNote: PHAsset.burstIdentifier/representsBurst and — powerfully — PHAsset.burstSelectionTypes let us READ Apple's own suggested-keeper flags (the gray dots) via a native bridge; expo-media-library's coverage of burst APIs is thin, so may need a small native module. Atlas flags this as a large, cheap storage win and a we-lead (Apple never nags).
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Memory MOVIE (auto-edited beat-synced music montage) needs AVFoundation composition/export + music — no Expo path (our Ken-Burns Slideshow gives the stills-playback experience; .mov export is native-only). Burst stacking needs PhotoKit burstIdentifier (unexposed); verify-then-delete depends on external import (blocked); Optimize-Storage iCloud original-fetch is a sync surface we deliberately opt out of.

feature: Duplicates detection + merge
appleBehavior: Collections → Utilities → Duplicates finds duplicate sets and Merge combines best pixels + union of relevant data (reversible via Recently Deleted). Famously slow to populate (days-to-weeks on large libraries), catches only near-exact dupes, undocumented criteria, and users can't see why two matched or force a re-scan.
userImpact: We ship a CLIP near-duplicate finder + merge — catching VISUAL near-dupes Apple misses, not just near-exact ones, and running on-device without Apple's multi-day populate lag. The atlas names dedupe 'the single biggest wedge' in the domain; we already occupy it.
feasibilityNote: Already implemented (CLIP embedding near-dup + merge). Opportunities to extend our lead: show WHY two matched, let users choose which copy survives, and a force-rescan — all things Apple can't do. PhotoKit exposes no Duplicates API, so this is entirely our own moat.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing

feature: Hidden album
appleBehavior: Hide moves items to a biometric-locked Hidden album that doesn't appear elsewhere in Photos; unhide after Face ID/Touch ID. (Not encryption — a discoverable location behind a gate; users wrongly think it's a vault.)
gap: No Hidden album, no hide action, no biometric-gated private area.
userImpact: Users can't hide sensitive photos from the main grid in our app; anyone scrolling sees everything.
feasibilityNote: The hardest PhotoKit wall (atlas §2.19): since iOS 16 the system won't return Hidden assets even with includeHiddenAssets, so we CANNOT browse the system Hidden album. Our only route is our OWN vault — import copies into app-private SQLCipher storage (we already have encrypted SQLite) + biometric gate — which the atlas notes could be a we-lead 'real encrypted vault' since Apple's Hidden isn't actually secure. Heavy/risky; decide early.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing

feature: Recently Deleted (30-day trash: view, recover, permanent-delete)
appleBehavior: Deleted items sit in a biometric-locked Recently Deleted collection for 30 days with Recover / Recover All / Delete All. Storage doesn't free for 30 days (a constant 'I deleted but storage didn't drop' confusion).
gap: We delete straight to the iOS system trash but do NOT surface Recently Deleted — no in-app trash view, no recover, no empty-trash, no 30-day messaging.
userImpact: After deleting in our app, users can't review/recover/purge from within it, and get no explanation that space won't free for 30 days. They must switch to Apple Photos to undo.
feasibilityNote: 'There is no API by which your app can fetch Recently Deleted assets' (Apple dev forums, atlas §2.19) — the system trash is completely inaccessible, so we can't list/recover/purge it. We CAN build our own soft-delete layer over the replica and clearly tell users Apple's 30-day trash is separate. We should at least surface the 30-day storage caveat at delete time (cheap trust win).

feature: Recovered collection (orphaned/unsaved-media quarantine)
appleBehavior: A separate safety net from Recently Deleted: copies of assets that couldn't be saved properly land in Utilities → Recovered, with Restore to Library / Permanently Delete (deletion is instantly irreversible, no notification, no grace).
gap: No Recovered surface and no proactive recovery of orphaned/partially-written media.
userImpact: The answer to a distressing class of 'my photos vanished' tickets — and there's a correctness angle: assets OUR OWN app fails to save could end up in Apple's Recovered. Proactively surfacing orphaned media would 'look like magic' (atlas §2.20).
feasibilityNote: No PHAssetCollectionSubtype for Recovered — inaccessible via PhotoKit. Actionable takeaway is defensive: robust save-completion handling on our writes so we don't dump user assets into Apple's Recovered. Our own equivalent would be an app-private recovery log.

feature: Liquid Glass grid chrome (translucent contextual tab/nav bar)
appleBehavior: Photos is a flagship Liquid Glass app: translucent tab bar/search/select buttons that show photos behind them and resize as you scroll. Known complaints: legibility over busy photos and controls that feel unstable as they resize.
userImpact: We deliberately ship a bold, opinionated vivid living-gradient identity (theme.ts/motion.tsx) instead of chasing Apple's Liquid Glass — the atlas's explicit strategic recommendation ('a bold, opinionated visual identity is rewarded'). We avoid Apple's legibility/instability complaints.
feasibilityNote: Intentional divergence; already shipped. We use pure RN Animated (no blur module), so we're not mimicking translucency — which the atlas endorses. No work needed.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing

feature: Star ratings + filter by rating (iOS 27 beta)
appleBehavior: iOS 27 beta adds 1–5 star ratings (enabled via a 'Show Ratings Controls' toggle; tap-hold or ⋯ → Rating) AND filtering the library by rating — the single most consequential iOS 27 browsing change.
gap: No ratings and no rate-based filtering.
userImpact: A core library primitive (rate then filter to your best) that we lack — and one we could ship on iOS 26 BEFORE Apple's stable release, a time-boxed opportunity.
feasibilityNote: Trivial in our own SQLite (rating column + filter), and confirmed current via web (idownloadblog/MacRumors, iOS 27 public beta July 2026). Interop wall: PHAsset.rating appears in PhotoKit's JSON but is unverified/unsurfaced (atlas §2.19), so we likely can't write Apple's rating — own-store only. Front-runs Apple's fall release.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Filter-by-rating (Library "Rated" filter, iOS-27-beta parity): replica ratedExternalIds(min=1) (parameterized SELECT over photo_meta) + a "Rated" pill in the Library filter row that keeps only star-rated photos. LIVE-VERIFIED (the Rated pill renders). Reviewed -> fixed P2 stale membership: threaded a ratingsVersion token PhotoGrid->PhotoDetail.onRate so an in-viewer rating change re-resolves the set + remounts the grid (ratings are app-local, no PhotoKit event). Star-rating INPUT already shipped in the viewer.

feature: Keywords (iOS 27 beta)
appleBehavior: iOS 27 beta: add keywords to a photo (info panel → scroll down → Add Keywords, with autocomplete); additive to captions, and filterable/searchable.
gap: No user keyword/tagging system.
userImpact: Users can't tag photos with their own vocabulary for organization/retrieval — the iOS 27 admission that captions alone weren't enough. We could serve this today.
feasibilityNote: Own-store keywords with autocomplete are straightforward over SQLite and could feed our search index. Same interop wall as captions — cannot round-trip into Apple's keyword field (blocked-platform for interop).
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Filter/browse BY KEYWORD (Library): replica keywordIndex() scans the prefs KV (photo.keywords.<id> JSON arrays) into distinct keyword labels + a lowercased-keyword -> external_id-set map; a horizontal keyword-chip row appears under the Library controls when scope=all and >=1 keyword exists, and tapping a chip narrows the grid (composes AFTER media/favorites/rated + screenshot-hide, folded into gridKey). Reviewed -> fixed P2 stale index after an in-app keyword edit: threaded a keywordsVersion token (PhotoGrid->PhotoDetail.editKeywords, mirroring the ratings token) into the index memo + gridKey. Keyword INPUT already shipped in the viewer.

feature: Captured by Me (iOS 27 beta Utilities collection)
appleBehavior: iOS 27 beta: a Utilities collection of only images actually shot with the Camera app (current or past iPhones), excluding screenshots and saved-from-others — an admission the library is polluted.
gap: No 'photos I actually took' view; screenshots and saved images are indistinguishable in our grid.
userImpact: Users who want to see only their own captures (not memes/screenshots/saved images) can't. A validated iOS 27 demand.
feasibilityNote: Approximate via PHAssetSourceType (.typeUserLibrary) + excluding photoScreenshot subtype + presence of camera EXIF — heuristic but effective, all from data we can read on-device. Pairs with the content-hiding toggles row.
domain: Library & Grid Browsing
closureNote: Infeasible for a 3rd-party app: capture-source "Captured by Me" + holiday-event metadata iOS does not expose; PhotoKit forbids non-destructive in-place edit (adjustmentData/Revert); intra-video key-moment CLIP needs a native frame-extraction pipeline; Android Motion Photo is N/A on iOS.

feature: Natural-language semantic search (core text->image)
appleBehavior: Apple Intelligence 'Natural language search in Photos' — describe a photo in words, matched against on-device image-language embeddings AND joined with the named-people index (e.g. 'Maya skateboarding in a tie-dye shirt'). Gated to iPhone 15 Pro / 16 / 17 only, 16 languages, unavailable in China mainland, still labelled 'beta'.
gap: We ship on-device CLIP ViT-B/32 text->image search fully offline with NO Apple-Intelligence hardware gate and no server hop — beating Apple on availability/privacy. Residual gap: Apple joins semantic matching with face identity, so person-conditioned queries ('<name> doing X') work for Apple and not for us; CLIP is also English-text-centric.
userImpact: Users on iPhone 14/15/15-Plus/SE — who get NOTHING from Apple's semantic search — get full semantic search from us. But 'photos of Dad at the beach' silently ignores 'Dad' because we have no on-device person join.
feasibilityNote: Already shipped (react-native-executorch CLIP + sqlite-vec). Person-conditioning needs a person index (needs-desktop oracle) fused with CLIP scores.
domain: Search (indexed dimensions, faces, OCR/Live Text, places, natural language, categories, captions, Visual Look Up)

feature: Person / people (named face) search
appleBehavior: Named people from the People & Pets collection are first-class search inputs; face identity is the backbone of Apple's best queries. No Apple Intelligence required for basic person-name search.
gap: No on-device face-identity search. The paired desktop can Recognize people per-photo (people chips) but it is NOT wired as a searchable dimension — you cannot type a name and get all their photos.
userImpact: The most-used real-world photo query ('pictures of my kid') is impossible in-app. This is the single biggest felt gap versus Apple.
feasibilityNote: Apple's own SDK gives NO face-recognition embedding to anyone (Vision = detection/landmarks/quality only), so this is structurally a desktop-oracle job (licensed embedder + clusterer); the person<->asset index must be computed on desktop and synced to the phone's SQLite to become a live search token.

feature: Live Text / OCR text-in-photo search (dimension 7)
appleBehavior: Recognized text inside photos (an email address, phone number, any words on a sign/receipt/screenshot) feeds Photos search AND system Spotlight. No Apple Intelligence required; hardware floor iPhone XS/XR; 46 locales.
gap: We do not OCR assets at all and cannot search text within photos. Finding the screenshot that says a specific word, or a receipt by its total, is impossible.
userImpact: Screenshot/receipt/document text search is a daily-driver query; its absence makes our search feel shallow and forces users back to Apple Photos.
feasibilityNote: RN/Expo has no Vision access; needs a native OCR module (VisionKit RecognizeTextRequest, ML Kit, or an executorch OCR model) to re-OCR every asset on-device, then index tokens in SQLite. Desktop could also OCR. Apple's already-computed OCR is not readable — you must re-OCR.
domain: Search (indexed dimensions, faces, OCR/Live Text, places, natural language, categories, captions, Visual Look Up)
closureNote: On-device OCR (ML Kit text-recognition) indexes the text inside every photo into replica photo_text (Unicode-lowercased, incremental, gated behind the semantic-search opt-in, degrades gracefully if unbuilt); Search unions text-in-photo matches with CLIP visual results. NEEDS a native rebuild.

feature: Date search (month or year)
appleBehavior: Type 'Date (month or year)' — e.g. 'December 2023' — to retrieve by capture date.
gap: Grid is date-desc only; no way to query or filter by a date, month, or year in Search.
userImpact: 'photos from last summer' is a routine query users expect; today they must scroll.
feasibilityNote: Capture date is already ingested (expo-media-library creationTime in SQLite). Adding date filters + light NL date parsing is trivial and needs no native module.
domain: Search (indexed dimensions, faces, OCR/Live Text, places, natural language, categories, captions, Visual Look Up)
closureNote: Search parses month/year (bare month needs a date preposition) → date-filtered results that work pre-CLIP, intersect with CLIP + favorites scope, and survive a tab switch.

appleBehavior: Type a 'Category' term; matched against a CLOSED, undocumented, fixed scene taxonomy. Queries outside it ('Rome monuments') silently return nothing; users can't see or extend the vocabulary.
gap: Our CLIP is open-vocabulary text->image, so arbitrary scene descriptions work — structurally beating Apple's closed taxonomy. Residual gap: no curated category browse/chips or scene suggestions to teach users what to type.
userImpact: We answer 'Rome monuments' where Apple draws a blank, but we give no visible category shortcuts, so discoverability of the capability is weaker.
feasibilityNote: Already shipped via CLIP. Could add curated category chips (client-side canned queries) cheaply.

appleBehavior: Type 'Events (sports games or concerts)'; Apple joins photo timestamp+location against an internal events knowledge base; coverage undocumented/spotty.
gap: No event retrieval.
