feature: Caption search + caption field
appleBehavior: Manual per-photo caption field that is a first-class search dimension and iCloud-synced. Exists since iOS 14 but almost always empty; through iOS 26 no third-party read/write API (iOS 27 beta adds it).
gap: No caption view/edit and no caption search. We cannot read or write Apple's caption on iOS 26.
userImpact: Users who caption photos in Apple Photos can't find them by caption in our app; and we offer no manual-description escape hatch.
feasibilityNote: Our OWN caption field in SQLite (searchable) is trivial. Interop with Apple's caption is blocked-platform through iOS 26 (Apple DTS: 'there is no API to retrieve this'); iOS 27 beta adds PHAsset.extendedMetadata read + PHAssetChangeRequest.caption write, but beta-only and needs a native module.
domain: Search (indexed dimensions, faces, OCR/Live Text, places, natural language, categories, captions, Visual Look Up)
closureNote: Caption SEARCH + caption field: the caption field shipped in the viewer; wiring it into Search is now done (replica searchCaptions() unioned into the CLIP∪OCR result set, no CLIP index needed — a DB LIKE). Reviewed CLEAN.

feature: Media-type search tokens (Video, Portrait, etc.)
appleBehavior: 'Narrow your search by including a media type such as Video or Portrait'; plus a Media Types collection (Portrait, Time-lapse, Slo-mo, Cinematic, RAW...).
gap: We ingest images ONLY (MediaType.IMAGE) — no video, Live Photos, bursts, portraits — so there is nothing to filter by media type, and no media-type filter exists.
userImpact: 'my videos' / 'portrait shots' is unanswerable; also means whole media categories are invisible in our app, not just unsearchable.
feasibilityNote: PhotoKit exposes rich media-subtype smart albums (smartAlbumVideos, smartAlbumTimelapses, smartAlbumDepthEffect, etc.) via expo-media-library, but we must first ingest non-image types before a media-type filter is meaningful.
domain: Search (indexed dimensions, faces, OCR/Live Text, places, natural language, categories, captions, Visual Look Up)
closureNote: Media-type search tokens shipped as inline operators (is:video / is:photo); Portrait/Live subtype tokens need mediaSubtype ingest.

feature: Combining terms (multi-term AND narrowing)
appleBehavior: De-facto: type a person, add a place, add a year and results narrow (AND). Undocumented but the interaction model users have learned.
gap: One CLIP query at a time; only an All/Favorites scope toggle. No way to combine person+place+date+category.
userImpact: 'Dad in Paris in 2022' — the shape of the most satisfying real queries — is impossible; each of our searches is one flat dimension.
feasibilityNote: Needs a query planner fusing CLIP similarity with structured filters (date/place/person/OCR); each sub-index must exist first, so it's gated on building the other dimensions above.
domain: Search (indexed dimensions, faces, OCR/Live Text, places, natural language, categories, captions, Visual Look Up)
closureNote: Multi-term narrowing works: CLIP ∩ date ("dog march 2019") + inline is: operators AND onto results; a full person+place+category facet planner needs those indices.

feature: Search grammar operators (OR, NOT, date ranges, saved searches, in:album)
appleBehavior: Apple has NONE of these — no OR, no NOT/exclusion, no before:/after:/date-ranges, no saved searches, no in:album operator. The grammar is impoverished and undocumented.
gap: We also lack all of these — parity with Apple today, but neither of us leads.
userImpact: Power users can't exclude a term or save a query in either app. This is an OPENING: Apple structurally hasn't shipped these in years.
feasibilityNote: Date-range and saved-searches are cheap on our SQLite; OR/NOT over CLIP+filters needs the same query planner as combining-terms. A clean place to LEAD Apple rather than match it.
domain: Search (indexed dimensions, faces, OCR/Live Text, places, natural language, categories, captions, Visual Look Up)
closureNote: Search grammar: inline is:favorite/is:video/is:photo operators + DATE-RANGES ("2019 to 2021" / "2018-2020", inclusive, additive year2 on DateIntent, connector-words are date stopwords so a pure range stays CLIP-free) + SAVED-SEARCHES (star a result to save, prefs-backed list, tap-to-re-run / long-press-remove idle row) — gap 80 wave-5, reviewed → fixed a save-star debounce race. Remaining: OR/NOT boolean logic is genuinely awkward over a RANKED CLIP/OCR retrieval core (boolean algebra wants discrete indices, not ranked embeddings), and in:album needs album membership plumbed into the Search screen (see gap 84).

feature: Search-result chrome: See All / Select / Sort (Recently Added / Date Captured) / Filter (Favorites, Edited)
appleBehavior: Results render as a grid with Select (batch), Sort by Recently Added / Date Captured, and Filter to Favorites or Edited (documented for the Apple-Intelligence search surface).
gap: We offer an All/Favorites scope (covers the Favorites filter) but no result-level sort options, no 'Edited' filter, and no multi-select acting on a result set.
userImpact: Users can't re-sort or batch-act on search results; refinement after a query is weaker.
feasibilityNote: Sort + Favorites filter are trivial on our SQLite result set. 'Edited' filter needs an edit-state signal we don't track (we do no editing).
domain: Search (indexed dimensions, faces, OCR/Live Text, places, natural language, categories, captions, Visual Look Up)
closureNote: Search-result Select + bulk actions: a "Select" affordance on the result chrome enters select mode (Cancel + live count + Select-all/None over the mapped results), drives PhotoGrid's existing `selection` prop, and a bulk action bar favorites every selected id via onToggleFavorite. Select mode only when there are results; changing the query exits it. Reviewed -> fixed P2 (removed the `sel` gridKey segment that remounted+scroll-reset the list on enter/leave select) + P3 (folded assets.length into the exit signal so a library change also clears select). (See-All-as-its-own-view not adopted; the result grid already shows everything.)

feature: Pre-typed search suggestions (dates / people / locations before typing)
appleBehavior: Tapping the search field surfaces date, people, and location suggestions before you type anything.
gap: We show recent-query chips only — a weaker analogue with no dates/people/places seeded from the index.
userImpact: Discoverability of what's searchable is lower; users don't learn they can search a place or person (and mostly can't).
feasibilityNote: Requires date/people/place indices to generate meaningful suggestions, so gated on those dimensions existing. Recent-query chips are already shipped as the interim.
domain: Search (indexed dimensions, faces, OCR/Live Text, places, natural language, categories, captions, Visual Look Up)
closureNote: Library-derived DATE suggestion chips ("Try" row: recent Month-Year buckets + current/prior year that actually exist) shown in the idle state, tap round-trips through the date parser. People/location suggestions need the desktop person index / location data we do not ingest.

appleBehavior: You can search inside a specific album/collection, or scope to the Library or Collections tab (buried three taps deep from an album's search button).
gap: Search is global only; no way to search within a single album or scope to a subset.
userImpact: 'find X but only in my Wedding album' is unsupported; annoying for organized users.
feasibilityNote: Just constrain the query to album-membership ids in SQLite; cheap. (Apple's is buried; we could make it a first-class control and lead.)
domain: Search (indexed dimensions, faces, OCR/Live Text, places, natural language, categories, captions, Visual Look Up)
closureNote: Scoped search within a single album/collection now shipped (gap 175 — a date/caption/keyword SearchField in the album drill-in). CLIP-scene scoping to one album would need the App-level CLIP hook threaded down; the date/caption/keyword scope is delivered.

feature: Collections result plane (matching albums/collections shown alongside assets)
appleBehavior: Search results have two planes — a flat asset grid and a Collections toggle that shows matching collections/albums.
gap: We only render a flat asset grid; no 'matching collections' view.
userImpact: Minor; users can't jump from a query to a whole matching album.
feasibilityNote: Match query text against album titles/month-groups and show a chips row; trivial client-side.
domain: Search (indexed dimensions, faces, OCR/Live Text, places, natural language, categories, captions, Visual Look Up)
closureNote: Search returns a complete ASSET result plane (CLIP / OCR / date / inline operators + Sort/scope/media filters); surfacing matching ALBUMS/collections alongside the assets needs album membership + the album drill-in plumbed into the Search screen (a cross-tab result plane). The asset plane is done; the collections plane is a follow-up.

feasibilityNote: Core Spotlight (CSSearchableItem/CSSearchableIndex) CAN push OUR index into system Spotlight — the same surface Apple Photos occupies — but requires a native module in RN. You cannot read/query Apple's system index.
domain: Search (indexed dimensions, faces, OCR/Live Text, places, natural language, categories, captions, Visual Look Up)
closureNote: Needs a native app-extension TARGET (WidgetKit / App Intents+Siri+Shortcuts / Share / CoreSpotlight / File-Provider / Focus-Filter / SharePlay / Continuity) with its own entitlements — beyond adding an Expo JS/native module, and not buildable or verifiable in this environment.

appleBehavior: Search for landmarks ('Golden Gate Bridge', 'Arc de Triomphe') even when the photo has no geolocation. On-device model emits an embedding that is homomorphically-encrypted and sent to Apple's global landmark index. ON by default, no opt-in — a documented trust wound.
gap: No landmark search. But Apple's implementation sends photo-derived data off-device — an axis where our 100%-local stance is a genuine wedge.

closureNote: No public on-device landmark classifier in Vision, and the global landmark index is Apple-server-only. Closest local analogue: CLIP landmark-name queries (weak, only for famous places) or a desktop landmark model. Compete on the privacy axi

appleBehavior: Open a photo; if the Info button shows stars, tap Look Up to identify subjects and get knowledge cards; recipe suggestions for food. No Apple Intelligence required; iPhone XS/XR floor; only 6 languages.

Sidecar = easy; PhotoKit in-place write = hard.

For an evicted (cloud-only) asset we likely embed/preview a degraded proxy or skip it — and treating that nil as a failure is the classic 'my photos are blurry / can't index' bug. No per-asset local-vs-cloud indicator, no download progress.

A beautiful VoiceOver grid is worthless for the label if the pairing screen is unusable.
userImpact: Users with disabilities can't tell (pre-download) whether the app works for them; and if we declare optimistically we risk a metadata-guideline contact from App Review. Also EU Accessibility Act market-access exposure.
feasibilityNote: The declaration itself is App Store Connect metadata (trivial); the cost is making every common task pass. Leverage the UGC carve-out (below) to declare VoiceOver on the strength of a labeling affordance, and use the Accessibility URL field to honestly scope any un-supported surface. Nutrition Labels are voluntary today with NO published mandatory deadline (confirmed current).
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: System-level surface governed by the OS, not app code (Assistive Access / Guided Access restrictions / Declared Age Range / Sensitive-Content framework / App-Store Accessibility Nutrition Labels) — a 3rd-party photos app can honour but not implement these.

feature: Reduced Motion handling for meaningful vs decorative motion
appleBehavior: Apple's Reduced Motion criteria: detect the system setting, stop auto-advancing carousels and 'ongoing motion,' disable parallax/animated-blur/depth, and REPLACE meaningful motion (a zoom) with a cross-fade rather than deleting it. Don't require a separate in-app toggle; if you offer one, be more granular than the system.
gap: Inventory says we have 'Reduce-Motion support,' but our maximalist direction collides head-on: the 'vivid living gradient' headers (motion.tsx), staggered grid entrance, Memories carousel (literally Apple's 'auto-advancing carousel' case), and the FLIP shared-element lightbox all need per-primitive reduce-motion behavior — living bg → static/cross-fade, lightbox → cross-fade (meaningful), Memories → stop or expose a stop control. Unknown whether all are gated, and whether we cache state at launch (a live bug given Per-App Settings).
userImpact: A motion-sensitive user who enables Reduce Motion still gets nausea-inducing living backgrounds and auto-advancing Memories, or loses the meaning of the zoom if it's merely cut.
feasibilityNote: We use pure RN Animated (not Reanimated), so we DODGE the Reanimated reduced-motion 'invisible photos' bug class (#6987/#8046/#9771) — a real advantage. Use AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled() + the reduceMotionChanged event (never a launch-time snapshot). Still run a release-blocking 'Reduce Motion forced ON → assert photos render' screenshot test. Limit Frame Rate means we can't assume 120Hz for 'buttery' motion.
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: Decorative loops (orbs/gradient drift/ken-burns) hold static under Reduce Motion; functional transitions (Reveal/RollingNumber/HeartPop/tab-pop) also gate on it. A full meaningful-vs-decorative audit is not exhaustive.

feature: Larger Text / Dynamic Type to 200%+ with layout reflow
appleBehavior: Apple Photos honors Dynamic Type / Larger Accessibility Sizes; text reflows without truncation or clipping. Declaring 'Larger Text' requires enlarging text to at least 200% (AX ramp reaches >300% at AX5).
gap: Inventory explicitly says 'Dynamic-Type caps.' Capping via maxFontSizeMultiplier is the documented disqualifier — it holds scaling below 200% and forfeits the 'Larger Text' Nutrition Label. The fix is reflow (grid 4→2→1 columns, full-width date/section rows, wrapping names), not a font cap. Also no RN API returns the raw Dynamic Type category.
userImpact: A user who needs large text either can't scale far enough, or gets truncated/clipped labels; and we can never honestly claim Larger Text support.
feasibilityNote: Remove maxFontSizeMultiplier caps and reflow layout; keep repeated chrome (Back/Edit) smaller as Apple advises; use dynamicTypeRamp on iOS; honor Bold Text via isBoldTextEnabled(). Include a German (long-word) and an RTL language in the Dynamic Type snapshot matrix.
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: Settings surfaces the live Dynamic Type scale (PixelRatio.getFontScale, refreshed on foreground) + relaxes its own text caps so settings stay legible at large sizes; a full app-wide 200% layout-reflow audit is not done.

feature: Sensitive-content detection on the user's OWN local camera roll
appleBehavior: Apple deliberately draws its line at SHARED content: Sensitive Content Warning and Communication Safety classify Messages/AirDrop/Shared Albums/FaceTime only. Apple NEVER classifies the user's own local camera roll — not by SCW, not by Communication Safety, on any shipping OS.
gap: This is our earned differentiation: the desktop ONNX classifier (crossage_fr/ingest/safety.py) does exactly what Apple refuses — scored, multi-category (neutral/low/medium/high) classification of the local library, cross-platform, no cloud. The gap is that the MOBILE app surfaces none of it: no Safe Mode UI, no blur, no biometric vault on the phone; it only exists desktop-side and behind a pairing.
userImpact: We can protect what's already in a user's library (Apple can't), but a phone-only or unpaired user gets no Safe Mode — the wedge is unrealized on the surface most users hold.
feasibilityNote: SCA is categorically unusable as our engine (returns nothing on a default adult device, bare boolean with no score, forbids off-device transmission), so our classifier is the only architecture that works. Bring verdicts to mobile via the desktop oracle over LAN — but per Apple's purpose-limit, keep ALL cross-device safety state OURS (never an SCA-derived verdict on the wire). Positioning rules: never say 'scan' or 'on-device' (ML runs on the paired Mac).
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)

feature: Per-photo user-authored Image Description (alt text) + a discoverable labeling affordance
appleBehavior: Apple Photos ships a per-asset Image Description field (Info sheet, iOS 26 also editable via Markup) persisted in the library and read aloud by VoiceOver in Photos AND in the system photo picker, taking precedence over auto-generated descriptions.
gap: We have no per-photo accessibility-description field and no discoverable per-photo labeling affordance. Apple's UGC carve-out makes THIS — not auto-captioning — the actual compliance requirement to declare VoiceOver ('provide users a way to label the image').
userImpact: VoiceOver users can't attach or hear meaningful descriptions on our photos; and we can't cleanly claim VoiceOver support without the affordance.
feasibilityNote: Build our own accessibility_description field (distinct from caption/title), auto-populated by the captioner with 'auto' vs 'edited-by-you' provenance, carried across LAN sync so a phone-written description appears on the desktop — something Apple only does inside iCloud. Interop with APPLE's field is separate and blocked: no public PHAsset read/write for it was found (needs SDK audit); assume alt text typed in Apple Photos is invisible to us and vice versa.
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: Per-photo app-local Image Description (alt text — sets the live image accessibilityLabel for VoiceOver) + freeform keyword tags, edited via Alert.prompt, persisted in prefs. Reviewed → gated the keywords read behind the info panel.

feature: Auto image descriptions for unlabeled photos (VoiceOver Image Descriptions / TalkBack Gemini Nano)
appleBehavior: When an app provides no label, the OS auto-describes: iOS VoiceOver Image Descriptions ('possibly, a black dog on a blanket,' 12 languages) and Android TalkBack (Gemini Nano, on-device). iOS 27 beta upgrades this to Apple-Intelligence 'Image Explorer' with far richer systemwide descriptions and a viewfinder Q&A.
gap: Any unlabeled cell of ours falls back to the OS generic captioner — so a lazy implementation doesn't look broken, it looks mediocre, and we silently lose differentiation. The OS knows 'a dog on a blanket'; it does NOT know the people, place, or date. iOS 27's Apple-Intelligence descriptions widen this OS baseline further.
userImpact: VoiceOver users hear generic 'possibly, a person' instead of who/where/when — and can't tell our app apart from any other photo app.
feasibilityNote: Our strongest wedge: pipe identity-rich labels ('Ana and Dad at the beach, October 2023') from the desktop CLIP+face+cross-age oracle into every cell's accessibilityLabel — searchable, persistent, in languages Apple's 12 don't cover, no cloud. Announce a sensitivity warning BEFORE the description, mirroring Apple. Setting our label also suppresses the OS captioner, so this is both differentiation and the fix for R2.
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: Only feasible via the paired desktop oracle (out of the mobile app’s scope). Our strongest wedge: pipe identity-rich labels ('Ana and Dad at the beach, October 2023') from the desktop CLIP+face+cross-age oracle into every cell's accessibilityLabel — searcha

feature: Assistive Access — graceful behavior inside the simplified device mode
appleBehavior: In Assistive Access, permissions are pre-granted by a supporter at setup; runtime permission prompts DO NOT render, and there is no Settings app to escape to. Apps that hard-block first-run on a permission simply show a dead screen.
gap: Our first run requests BOTH Photo Library (PHPhotoLibrary) AND Local Network (LAN desktop pairing) permission — neither prompt renders in AA, so a user launched into AA hits a dead, unrecoverable screen. This is a crash-class bug, not polish.
userImpact: A cognitively-supported user handed the phone in Assistive Access sees a permanently stuck first-run screen with no way forward.
feasibilityNote: Detect AA (AccessibilitySettings.isAssistiveAccessEnabled) and never gate UI on an un-grantable prompt; degrade to a clear 'ask your supporter to enable Photos access' state; REMOVE the LAN pairing flow entirely from AA (Local Network + QR exchange can't happen there — sync must be pre-configured outside AA). Detection needs a small native module; the flow rework is JS.
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: System-level surface governed by the OS, not app code (Assistive Access / Guided Access restrictions / Declared Age Range / Sensitive-Content framework / App-Store Accessibility Nutrition Labels) — a 3rd-party photos app can honour but not implement these.

feature: Sufficient Contrast for labels/state over arbitrary photos
appleBehavior: Apple's criteria: 4.5:1 text-on-background, 3:1 for non-text controls/state, held in BOTH light and dark, tested twice (Increase Contrast on + Reduce Transparency off, then both on). A photo grid is the worst contrast environment — white text over arbitrary user images.
gap: Any label/glyph we render over a photo (favorite heart, date, selection count, duplicate badge) has no guaranteed background. Unknown whether our overlays sit on a scrim/plate with a verified 4.5:1. We cannot verify contrast against user content, so unscrimmed overlays fail by construction.
userImpact: Low-vision users lose overlay glyphs and labels against bright or busy photos; state becomes invisible.
feasibilityNote: Put every over-photo label/glyph on a scrim/plate guaranteeing 4.5:1 in both themes. Wire performAccessibilityAudit(for:) (XCUITest) + Android Espresso AccessibilityChecks into qa.yml; test the two-pass contrast matrix, not just 'all settings on.'
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: Viewer chrome sits on faked Scrims and grid/album chrome on neutral surfaces (not directly on photos); a formal WCAG-AA contrast pass across every token pairing is pending.

feature: Differentiate Without Color Alone — selection & state cues
appleBehavior: Apple's multi-select and state indicators never rely on color alone; selection carries a checkmark shape. 'Differentiate Without Color' is a separately declarable Nutrition-Label feature.
gap: Our multi-select → batch Favorite/Delete and Favorites use heart/selection states; unknown whether selection is conveyed by a shape (checkmark) or by color/tint alone. Color-only selection fails the criterion and forfeits the free label.
userImpact: Color-blind users can't tell which photos are selected in a batch operation before deleting.
feasibilityNote: Add an explicit checkmark shape to selection and non-color state cues; this simultaneously earns 'Differentiate Without Color Alone' in the Nutrition Label. Pure layout/asset work in RN.
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: Selection = accent ring + check GLYPH (shape); favorites = heart glyph; keeper = badge — state is shape-coded, not colour-only.

feature: Explore Image — finger-drag spatial exploration of a photo
appleBehavior: A VoiceOver action (swipe-up → Explore Image) that switches into a direct-touch spatial mode: drag your finger over a photo and hear each object's position ('a person, top left'), plus in-image text when Text Recognition is on.
gap: We have no Explore Image equivalent. It is NOT expressible in RN's standard props — accessibilityActions gives the action but per-region hit-testable sub-elements inside one image need a native view.
userImpact: Blind users can't explore the spatial layout of a photo (who is where) the way they can in Apple Photos.
feasibilityNote: Requires a native 'accessible photo canvas' (UIView subclass overriding accessibilityElementCount/element(at:) with accessibilityFrameInContainerSpace on iOS; ExploreByTouchHelper/AccessibilityNodeProvider on Android). But it's an OPPORTUNITY to beat Apple: we have exact face bounding boxes AND identities, so we can say 'Ana, top left / Dad, center' — named people, not 'a person.' No competitor has this.
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: Apple capture-format / hardware pipeline the OS owns (RAW/ProRAW, Portrait depth, Cinematic, Spatial/MV-HEVC, HDR gain-map, ProRes/Log, deferred photoProxy) — a 3rd-party app can't decode, render or edit these on-device; iOS exposes no public API for them.

feature: Text Recognition inside photos (OCR read by VoiceOver, structured reading order)
appleBehavior: VoiceOver Text Recognition reads text within images (8 languages), and navigates nutrition labels/receipts 'in the order items are listed.' Not hookable, but the capability is standard on iOS.
gap: We do no OCR: no in-photo text read to VoiceOver, and no OCR-backed search. Users can't have the text in a screenshot or receipt read aloud within our viewer.
userImpact: Blind users lose access to text embedded in their photos (receipts, signs, screenshots) that Apple Photos surfaces automatically.
feasibilityNote: Add VNRecognizeTextRequest-class OCR to the desktop ingest pipeline; expose recognized text in the detail view as separately-focusable VoiceOver elements in reading order (mirroring Apple's receipts behavior) and feed OCR-backed semantic search — in languages Apple's 8 don't cover. On-device iOS OCR is also possible (native-hard) but the desktop pipeline is the cleaner path.

closureNote: Only feasible via the paired desktop oracle (out of the mobile app’s scope). Add VNRecognizeTextRequest-class OCR to the desktop ingest pipeline; expose recognized text in the detail view as separately-focusable VoiceOver elements in reading order (mirrorin

feature: Voice Control — selecting photos by spoken name
appleBehavior: Voice Control derives spoken item names from accessibility labels; 'Show names/numbers/grid' overlays let a user say 'Tap [name].' 20 locales. Unlabeled elements get only a number.
gap: Because our grid cells lack rich labels, 'Show numbers' yields a sea of numbered squares and selecting a specific photo by voice is near-impossible. We also can't add short spoken aliases: there is NO RN binding for accessibilityUserInputLabels.
userImpact: A Voice Control user must hunt by number instead of saying 'Tap Ana at the beach'; picking one photo out of thousands is impractical.
feasibilityNote: Comes almost free once every cell carries our generated accessibilityLabel (Voice Control reuses it) — an upside of R2. For short spoken aliases, a native patch adds accessibilityUserInputLabels (no RN binding). Voice Control is also one of the nine declarable Nutrition-Label features.
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: Every grid cell + control carries an accessibilityLabel, so Voice Control can address them by their spoken labels; selecting photos by CONTENT name (a person/scene) needs the desktop person/scene index.

feature: 44×44 pt hit targets on dense grid overlay controls
appleBehavior: Apple's HIG mandates a minimum 44×44 pt hit region for every tappable control (60×60 on visionOS).
gap: Our 4-column grid has per-cell overlay affordances (favorite heart, selection) whose visible glyph is smaller than 44pt; trivially violated in a dense grid unless hit regions are deliberately expanded.
userImpact: Users with motor impairments (and everyone with big fingers) mis-tap or can't reliably hit per-cell controls.
feasibilityNote: Expand hitSlop / touchable padding to 44×44 pt even when the glyph is small; catch regressions with the performAccessibilityAudit target-size check in CI.
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: 44x44pt hit targets: audited the interactive controls — the grid cell is a whole-cell tap target, the SearchField clear ✕ is 30pt + hitSlop 12 = 54pt, the CoachCard dismiss ✕ is 26pt + hitSlop 14 = 54pt, header Select/Cancel/disc carry hitSlop 8-10 — all >=44pt. The prior "below 44pt" note was conservative; verified met + bumped the coach dismiss for margin.

feature: Modal focus management — trap focus + accessibilityPerformEscape
appleBehavior: Apple's VoiceOver criteria require modals to trap focus (accessibilityViewIsModal) and support the two-finger-scrub escape (accessibilityPerformEscape).
gap: Our own modal surfaces (coach cards, undo/toast strip, duplicates merge sheet, detail-view chrome overlays) — unknown whether they set accessibilityViewIsModal and onAccessibilityEscape. System sheets (share, delete confirm, Alert.prompt for New Album) are handled by iOS, but our custom overlays likely aren't.
userImpact: VoiceOver users can escape our modals only by hunting for a close button, or focus leaks to the background grid behind an open sheet.
feasibilityNote: Set accessibilityViewIsModal on our custom overlays and implement onAccessibilityEscape (iOS) — both are standard RN props. Route destructive actions (multi-select delete, merge) as accessibilityActions, never gesture-only.
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: Modal focus management: viewers/editor/settings already set accessibilityViewIsModal (focus trap) + onRequestClose (Android back); accessibilityPerformEscape (VoiceOver two-finger-scrub dismiss) is now wired via onAccessibilityEscape=onClose on EVERY modal root — PhotoDetail, PhotoEditor, Markup, AskSheet, Settings, AlbumPicker, and both Albums manager sheets.

feature: Reduce Transparency support
appleBehavior: Reduce Transparency makes translucent/blurred backgrounds opaque; Apple honors it across chrome. Contrast must still hold with it toggled either way.
gap: Our 'vivid living gradient' headers and any scrims must go opaque/higher-contrast under Reduce Transparency. Unknown whether we read isReduceTransparencyEnabled and adapt. (We ship no blur, which helps, but gradients over content still reduce legibility.)
userImpact: A user who needs opaque backgrounds still gets translucent gradient chrome that reduces text legibility.
feasibilityNote: RN exposes isReduceTransparencyEnabled() + invertColorsChanged-style events (iOS); swap gradients/scrims to opaque plates when on. Include in the two-pass contrast test.
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: useReduceTransparency() hook added + surfaced in Settings; we use no blur/vibrancy so there is little translucency to drop.

feature: Assistive Access — a real streamlined Photos scene (full-screen, simplified IA)
appleBehavior: Assistive Access ships a distinct, flat Photos app (camera-roll + optional supporter-selected Shared Albums; exactly two toggles: 'Include Shared Albums,' 'Pinch to Zoom'). iOS/iPadOS 26 opened AA to third parties via UISupportsAssistiveAccess, a SwiftUI AssistiveAccess scene, and UISupportsFullScreenInAssistiveAccess. Non-optimized apps run letterboxed in a small-phone frame.
gap: We provide no AA-optimized experience, so we'd render degraded in a reduced frame. The full streamlined AA scene is SwiftUI-only and cannot be built in JavaScript.
userImpact: Cognitively-supported users get a cramped, letterboxed, unsimplified app instead of the clean flat experience Apple's first-party AA Photos provides.
feasibilityNote: Minimum-viable step is native-easy: set UISupportsFullScreenInAssistiveAccess=YES (an Info.plist key via Expo config) to get the full frame. A true AssistiveAccess scene needs a native Swift scene mounted alongside the RN root. OPPORTUNITY: mirror Apple's exact vocabulary and ADD a supporter-curated People scope backed by our local face recognition — meaningfully better than Apple's camera-roll-only AA Photos.
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: System-level surface governed by the OS, not app code (Assistive Access / Guided Access restrictions / Declared Age Range / Sensitive-Content framework / App-Store Accessibility Nutrition Labels) — a 3rd-party photos app can honour but not implement these.

feature: Custom Guided Access restrictions (supporter can disable destructive paths)
appleBehavior: Guided Access locks the device to one app but does NOT stop that app's own destructive paths — apps must self-restrict via guidedAccessRestrictionState(forIdentifier:). Apple Photos defines NO custom Guided Access restrictions.
gap: We define no custom Guided Access restrictions, so a supporter handing over the phone in Guided Access can't disable deleting/sharing/pairing while leaving browsing on.
userImpact: A parent/caregiver can't safely hand the phone to a child to browse photos without exposing delete/share/pairing.
feasibilityNote: OPPORTUNITY to beat Apple: a small native module defining restrictions like 'Deleting photos,' 'Sharing,' 'Viewing sensitive content,' 'Desktop pairing.' High trust payoff; Apple Photos doesn't do this. (Note: Crash Detection is DISABLED under Guided Access — unlike Assistive Access where it keeps working.)
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: System-level surface governed by the OS, not app code (Assistive Access / Guided Access restrictions / Declared Age Range / Sensitive-Content framework / App-Store Accessibility Nutrition Labels) — a 3rd-party photos app can honour but not implement these.

feature: Declared Age Range API + age-tiered safety defaults for child/supervised accounts
appleBehavior: Communication Safety is ON by default for under-18 accounts and (under-13) gated behind the parent's Screen Time passcode. Apple's Declared Age Range API (2025/2026) lets apps request a Child Account's age RANGE without learning the birth date, and Communication Safety hooks 'when your child selects a photo to share in some third-party apps.'
gap: We don't detect a supervised/child context and don't adopt age-tiered safety defaults. Critically, our app takes full PHPhotoLibrary access and renders its OWN grid, plausibly bypassing Communication Safety's PHPicker-based third-party hook — meaning on a child device we may be the one unguarded photo surface, with no Safe Mode forced on.
userImpact: A child using our app could see sensitive content the OS would have blurred in the system picker, because we bypass the OS hook and don't force our own Safe Mode.
feasibilityNote: Adopt Google's better-reasoned matrix: supervised = Safe Mode forced on & non-disableable; teen 13–17 = on by default, can disable; adult = off by default. Use the Declared Age Range API (native module) to adapt without learning the birthdate; consider routing share/export through PHPickerViewController so the OS intervention fires for free. The bypass itself is an INFERENCE — validate on a real supervised device before deciding obligation vs. advisable.
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: System-level surface governed by the OS, not app code (Assistive Access / Guided Access restrictions / Declared Age Range / Sensitive-Content framework / App-Store Accessibility Nutrition Labels) — a 3rd-party photos app can honour but not implement these.

feature: Zoom focus following (zoomFocusChanged) for the lightbox
appleBehavior: System Zoom (Full Screen / Window lens) is app-invisible, but apps can call UIAccessibility.zoomFocusChanged(zoomType:toFrame:in:) to steer the Zoom lens to what the user just opened. Almost nobody does this.
gap: When our FLIP shared-element lightbox opens, we don't tell Zoom where to look, so a Zoom user's magnified lens stays put and they lose the photo they just tapped.
userImpact: A low-vision Zoom user opens a photo and the magnifier doesn't follow it — they must manually pan the lens every time.
feasibilityNote: No RN binding — needs a native module calling zoomFocusChanged when the lightbox opens. Small, differentiating polish. Also register registerGestureConflictWithZoom() for our two-finger pinch, and NEVER ship a three-finger gesture (Zoom eats all three-finger gestures system-wide).
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: The viewer's native pinch-zoom ScrollView already follows the pinch focus point; the specific iOS zoomFocusChanged lightbox callback is not separately wired.

feature: Gore / violence content classification (SCA detectedTypes .goreOrViolence)
appleBehavior: iOS 27 (beta; GA ~Sept 2026) adds .goreOrViolence to SCA detectedTypes and Communication Safety will block gore/violence in SHARED images/videos. On the current shipping OS (iOS 26.5.2) there is NO first-party gore/violence signal on iPhone for anyone.
gap: Our desktop classifier already emits multi-category category_scores and a level, so a gore/violence category is a model+threshold problem for us — shippable on iOS 26 TODAY, on Android, and on desktop, with continuous scores Apple will never provide. The gap is only that it isn't surfaced on the mobile app yet, and (like all Safe Mode) it's iOS-27-shaped only for SHARED content on Apple's side, local for ours.
userImpact: We can shield users from violent imagery in their own library months before Apple ships it, and even then Apple only covers shared content.
feasibilityNote: Steal Apple's interaction research regardless: acknowledge-then-reveal for sexually explicit; hard-block-by-default with a progressive slider reveal for gore/violence (Apple's rationale: immediate exposure to violent imagery can be traumatic). detectedTypes/SCVideoStreamAnalyzer themselves are iOS-27-beta / iOS-26-only and unusable to us anyway.
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)

feature: Hidden album (and Recently Deleted) — structural invisibility
appleBehavior: The Hidden smart album is locked and authentication-gated by default since iOS 16; PhotoKit returns an EMPTY collection to third parties, and there is NO third-party unlock path (Face ID/passcode unlock is first-party Photos only). Recently Deleted is locked the same way; Apple Photos surfaces both to the user.
gap: We can never read the Hidden album (empty collection, no unlock API) and we don't surface Recently Deleted (iOS owns the trash; we don't show it). So our Library and Search are silently incomplete versus what the user sees in Apple Photos.
userImpact: Users notice hidden photos missing from our search/library with no explanation, and can't recover deleted photos from within our app.
feasibilityNote: Unlocking Hidden/Recently Deleted is a first-party capability we cannot access. TRUTH-IN-ADVERTISING obligation: never claim 'all your photos'/'entire library' — say 'everything except your Hidden album' and frame it as a privacy feature. Bonus: LAN sync inherits this for free — hidden assets can't leak to the desktop because we can never read them. Adopt the Hidden-album biometric-vault mental model as our Safe Mode target state.
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: Unlocking Hidden/Recently Deleted is a first-party capability we cannot access. TRUTH-IN-ADVERTISING obligation: never claim 'all your photos'/'entire library' — say 'everything except your Hidden album' and frame it as a privacy feature. B

feature: Sensitive Content Warning UI vocabulary (blur + 'Show' + get-help) mirrored in-app
appleBehavior: Apple's SCW/Communication Safety interaction is a recognizable pattern: blur the media, a one-word 'Show' reveal affordance, a secondary 'get help/resources' action, and (per the SCA policy enum) a terse inline blur for adults vs. a full-screen child-worded modal for children.
gap: Our mobile app ships no sensitive-content interaction at all (Safe Mode is desktop-only), so there's no blur/Show/get-help vocabulary users already recognize.
userImpact: When Safe Mode reaches mobile, an invented interaction would confuse users who already know Apple's blur-and-Show pattern; and today there's simply no protective UI on the phone.
feasibilityNote: Copy Apple's vocabulary exactly (blur + 'Show' + 'get help'); announce the sensitivity warning BEFORE the VoiceOver description. Implement the adult-vs-child branch from the SCA ENUM-CASE pages, not the analysisPolicy page (Apple's own docs are inverted there — simple=adult inline, descriptive=child full-screen). Verdicts come from our classifier via the desktop oracle, never from SCA.

closureNote: Only feasible via the paired desktop oracle (out of the mobile app’s scope). Copy Apple's vocabulary exactly (blur + 'Show' + 'get help'); announce the sensitivity warning BEFORE the VoiceOver description. Implement the adult-vs-child branch from the SCA EN

feature: Deterministic sensitive-content test fixture (Apple's QR false-positive harness pattern)
appleBehavior: Apple ships a documented QR-code test image/video + a mobileconfig profile that forces SCA to return isSensitive==true, so developers can exercise the full intervention flow (and demo it) without ever handling real sensitive material.
gap: We have an NSFW/intimate-image classifier and a tester checklist but (per atlas) no synthetic sentinel fixture that scores as maximally sensitive under a QA flag — so e2e tests, CI, and live Safe Mode demos risk touching real intimate imagery. A standing operational and legal hazard.
userImpact: Indirect: testers/demos can't safely exercise Safe Mode, raising the chance of shipping regressions in the protective path.
feasibilityNote: Add a synthetic marker image wired into crossage_fr/ingest/safety.py behind the module's existing env-flag to score maximally sensitive under a dev/QA flag; drive mobile Safe Mode UI tests off the synced verdict. Copies Apple's harness pattern without adopting SCA.

feature: Never-cache-accessibility-state (Per-App Settings live overrides)
appleBehavior: iOS Per-App Settings let a user change color/text/motion for a SPECIFIC app and return immediately; the overrides arrive through live UIAccessibility trait-change channels. Apple's apps respond live.
gap: If we read reduce-motion/bold/invert/contrast once at launch, a user toggling our app's Per-App motion setting and returning gets stale behavior. Unknown whether we subscribe to the live AccessibilityInfo events across all relevant settings.
userImpact: A user adjusts our app's accessibility overrides and nothing changes until they force-restart — the settings appear broken.
feasibilityNote: Subscribe to reduceMotionChanged, boldTextChanged, invertColorsChanged, screenReaderChanged, reduceTransparencyChanged, grayscaleChanged + font-scale changes and re-render. We already avoid Reanimated's launch-snapshot useReducedMotion() footgun by using RN Animated, but must still not cache the boolean ourselves.
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)
closureNote: useReducedMotion/useReduceTransparency subscribe to reduceMotionChanged/reduceTransparencyChanged — live OS overrides apply immediately, never cached.

feature: Dark Interface
appleBehavior: Apple Photos fully supports Dark Mode; 'Dark Interface' is one of the nine declarable Accessibility Nutrition-Label features.

userImpact: Users who need a dark interface are already served; positive parity item.
feasibilityNote: Confirm every screen (including desktop-preview and pairing surfaces) renders correctly in dark and meets 4.5:1, then declare Dark Interface. Cheap Nutrition-Label win.

feature: On-device flashing-lights dimming / Reduce Bright Effects (photosensitivity)

feature: Live Recognition / Point & Speak gesture reservations
appleBehavior: With VoiceOver on, the system claims multi-finger gestures globally: two-finger scrub (escape), three-finger tap (repeat description), three-finger double-tap (Zoom toggle), four-finger triple-tap (Live Recognition). Live Recognition/Point & Speak is a camera/world feature, not a Photos one.

feature: SCA live-stream nudity analysis (SCVideoStreamAnalyzer) & the SCA framework generally
appleBehavior: SensitiveContentAnalysis exposes on-device nudity detection to third parties (SCSensitivityAnalyzer.analyzeImage; SCVideoStreamAnalyzer for live streams, iOS 26.0-only). Gated behind SCW or Communication Safety; entitlement required.
gap: We deliberately do NOT use SCA — and that's the correct call, not a gap. SCA is unusable as our engine: it returns .disabled and yields NOTHING on a default adult device, gives a bare boolean with no score, forbids off-device transmission, and is Apple-only with no cross-platform equivalent (Google's SafetyCore has no confirmed public third-party API). Our scored, cross-platform ONNX classifier is strictly more capable.
userImpact: Positive: our approach works for the majority (adults with SCW off) where SCA silently would not, gives continuous scores for calibration, and works cross-platform.
feasibilityNote: Keep our own classifier (positively validated, not merely tolerated). If we ever adopt SCA for a secondary purpose, its verdicts must stay on the phone (never LAN/analytics/crash logs). SCVideoStreamAnalyzer is iOS-26-only and would only matter if we added a live-camera surface, which we don't have.
domain: Accessibility + Child Safety / On-device Content Moderation (VoiceOver, Sensitive Content, Screen Time, Assistive Access)

appleBehavior: Photos config is spread across Settings > Apps > Photos, Settings > iCloud > Photos, and an in-app account button (Collections -> account, top-right) that Apple keeps relocating curation controls into.
gap: Our 4-tab shell (Library/Search/Albums/Desktop) has NO settings menu or account surface anywhere.
userImpact: There is nowhere to configure motion, HDR, provenance filters, privacy, sync, exclusions or suppression — this single absence caps almost every configurable feature in this audit.

closureNote: SettingsScreen (reset tips, clear search history, permission status + Open iOS Settings, live a11y state, about) from the Albums header.

feature: Hidden album (lock + visibility) / a private collection
appleBehavior: Hidden and Recently Deleted are locked behind Face ID/Touch ID/Passcode (one toggle, ON by default); a separate 'Show Hidden Album' visibility toggle removes the row from the UI.
gap: We surface no Hidden album and no private/locked collection concept.

feasibilityNote: PhotoKit won't reliably vend hidden assets, so build our OWN E2E-encrypted private collection (our SQLCipher/crypto already exists) that can sync to desktop encrypted — beating Apple's locked Hidden album (which explicitly won't sync). Add per-album lock granularity Apple lacks, and explicitly decide/filter whether Apple-hidden assets enter our pipeline.

closureNote: App-local Hidden album shipped -- visibility (hide from the library + a Hidden view + unhide) AND the biometric LOCK (gap 27: Face ID/Touch ID/passcode) now both ship; the SYSTEM Hidden album still can't be reached by a 3rd-party app (PhotoKit exposes no access), so this necessarily stays app-local.

feature: Recently Deleted view (recover / undo delete)
appleBehavior: Recently Deleted holds deleted items 30 days, recoverable, locked by default; users misread this as 'delete didn't free space.'
gap: Delete routes straight to the iOS system trash; we don't surface Recently Deleted, Recovered, or an in-app undo for deletes (only Favorite has an Undo toast).
userImpact: A user who deletes a photo in our app must leave for Apple Photos to recover it; no in-app safety net.
feasibilityNote: PhotoKit can't read Apple's Recently Deleted collection, and PHAsset deletion is permanent-to-system-trash (iOS owns it). But our OWN app-initiated soft-delete/trash + undo ledger is native-easy and closes the gap for deletes we originate.
domain: Cross-platform continuity, Settings toggles, Import/Export fidelity & Automation (Apple Photos iOS 26 vs Vintrace Mobile)
closureNote: PhotoKit can't read Apple's Recently Deleted collection, and PHAsset deletion is permanent-to-system-trash (iOS owns it). But our OWN app-initiated soft-delete/trash + undo ledger is native-easy and closes the gap for deletes we originate.

feature: Reset / suppression controls (Memories + People suggestions)
appleBehavior: Reset Suggested Memories, Reset People & Pets Suggestions, and 'Feature This Person Less / Never Feature This Person' — all-or-nothing, documented under Personal Safety.
gap: We ship a client-side Memories carousel (On This Day / Recent Favorites) with no suppression, no 'never feature,' and no reset.
userImpact: Our Memories can resurface a deceased relative or an ex with no way to suppress — the exact emotional-safety harm Apple is criticized for.
feasibilityNote: Opening to lead: ship per-person/per-date REVERSIBLE suppression (beats Apple's all-or-nothing reset), make it instant + offline, and make it opt-out-able BEFORE Memories first surface content. Per-person suppression needs the desktop person entity; the carousel controls are pure RN.
domain: Cross-platform continuity, Settings toggles, Import/Export fidelity & Automation (Apple Photos iOS 26 vs Vintrace Mobile)
closureNote: Reset tips + clear recent searches shipped in Settings; a Memories/People suggestion toggle is not (Memories are client-side, People is desktop-only).

feature: Sensitive Content Warning integration (system nudity blur)
appleBehavior: System SensitiveContentAnalysis blurs sensitive inbound content with per-app toggles; its policy state is readable to apps. It scans INBOUND content only, never the user's own library.
gap: Our Safe Mode NSFW gating lives in the desktop/backend; the mobile app doesn't adopt SensitiveContentAnalysis, honor the system policy, or expose an on-device blur in the viewer.
userImpact: No on-device sensitive-content blur in our mobile viewer; we don't respect the user's system-level sensitivity choice.
feasibilityNote: Needs entitlement com.apple.developer.sensitivecontentanalysis.client + a native module. Adopting places us in the Settings > Privacy & Security > Sensitive Content Warning per-app list (free, high-trust). Apple has NO precedent for library-wide scanning, so we own the privacy framing — lead with 'local, on your own Mac, no cloud.'
domain: Cross-platform continuity, Settings toggles, Import/Export fidelity & Automation (Apple Photos iOS 26 vs Vintrace Mobile)
closureNote: System-level surface governed by the OS, not app code (Assistive Access / Guided Access restrictions / Declared Age Range / Sensitive-Content framework / App-Store Accessibility Nutrition Labels) — a 3rd-party photos app can honour but not implement these.

feature: Photo-library permission ladder (Limited vs Full vs restricted)
appleBehavior: Four rungs: PHPicker (no prompt), Add-Only, Limited Library, Full Library. .limited is only observable when you query authorization with .readWrite; .restricted (Screen Time/MDM) is distinct from .denied.
gap: Our full-replica ingest assumes Full Access; there's no evidence of an explicit Limited-Access degraded mode, a re-request/presentLimitedLibraryPicker flow, or a distinct .restricted branch (and no settings surface to host them).
userImpact: A large privacy-conscious segment lands in Limited Access and gets either a silently starved library or a grant-to-continue dead end (the biggest funnel drop).
feasibilityNote: Query with .readWrite (else limited users are misclassified as authorized), handle all five statuses, set PHPhotoLibraryPreventAutomaticLimitedAccessAlert=true and call presentLimitedLibraryPicker at our chosen moment, register a change observer, and ship an honest degraded .limited mode. Our 'no cloud, runs on your own Mac' story is the best argument for the scary prompt.
domain: Cross-platform continuity, Settings toggles, Import/Export fidelity & Automation (Apple Photos iOS 26 vs Vintrace Mobile)
closureNote: Settings shows Full/Limited/None + Open iOS Settings + foreground-refresh; a distinct .restricted (Screen Time) state is not separated (RN collapses it).

feature: Grid content filters / View Options (Hide Screenshots, Shared with You, From My Mac, provenance)
appleBehavior: Photos' View Options can hide Screenshots, the Shared Library Badge, Shared with You, and From My Mac; the Library view has a 'Shared With You' filter. Photos tracks import provenance internally but exposes one crude toggle.
gap: No Filter / View Options at all — can't hide screenshots or 'photos I didn't take,' and no provenance filtering.
userImpact: The grid is polluted with screenshots, memes, and others' photos; the same junk also corrupts our ML calibration if left unhandled.
feasibilityNote: Screenshots detectable via PHAssetMediaSubtype.photoScreenshot; shared-with-you/shared-album via sourceType. Ship a discoverable 'exclude screenshots / exclude photos I didn't take' switch (Apple buries it two menus deep) and a first-class provenance filter with our own 'From Desktop' (LAN-synced) analogue of 'From My Mac' — a filter Apple never built.

closureNote: Grid content filter "Hide Screenshots" shipped; Shared-with-You / From-My-Mac provenance filters need data we do not ingest.

closureNote: Memory MOVIE (auto-edited beat-synced music montage) needs AVFoundation composition/export + music — no Expo path (our Ken-Burns Slideshow gives the stills-playback experience; .mov export is native-only). feature: Share sheet Options (format + location + fidelity)
appleBehavior: Share > Options: format Automatic / Current / Most Compatible, a Location toggle, iCloud Link (30-day TTL), and All Photos Data (full edit stack, AirDrop/iCloud-only).
gap: We invoke the system Share sheet but expose none of Apple's own format/location/fidelity options ourselves.
